name: Turn/step loop exposed as typed waterfalls
what: A turn is zero or more steps (one model request plus its tool calls). Every phase is a documented interception point, so policy, hooks, UI and recovery attach without patching the loop.
how: Durable session events turn/* and step/*; live waterfalls agent/pre-step, agent/request, llm/stream, tools/pre-execute, tools/execute, tools/post-execute and agent/request-error; serial agent/turn-stopping. One concrete driver (ReactLoopAgent) registers itself as the AgentFactory on ctx.agents; consumers never import it. Waterfall listeners must call next() or they short-circuit.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane's execution-core step loop could publish the same phase list (pre-step, request, request-error recovery, turn-stopping) as a typed hook contract instead of fixed inline hooks.
notes: Prior Verevon analysis (4.1) captured the shape; the additions are the separate recovery phase (agent/request-error), the serial stop checkpoint, and the explicit rule that a loop change must update docs/architecture.md.

name: One durable inbox with next-turn / next-step targets and a wake flag
what: All pending input (prompts, steering, injected context, job notices, subagent messages) enters one inbox that decides whether it opens a turn or joins the next step. Pending work is readable and editable without a live agent.
how: Agent.send(message, target, wakeup) with followup/steer/inject as fixed-preset aliases. Every inbox mutation commits one normalized agent/inbox/spliced event folded by a projection; claiming is a splice without an outcome (the durable event is still agent/inbox/spliced; agent/inbox/claimed is the live notification), discards carry outcome 'canceled'. MessageId is unique across both lists. Cancel clears the inbox unless keepInbox is set. Verified in source: the fold rejects out-of-range splices and any MessageId pending in both lists; mutate normalizes negative and NaN offsets before logging.
verevonRelevance: A single durable inbox abstraction could replace ad-hoc queue/steer handling across Model Plane run controls and let the Frontend Plane show pending work from projections.
notes: Known gaps: no durable parent mailbox for subagent replies, a wake gap during cancellation convergence, and a settlement inside the retirement window can strand a job notice (tool-jobs README).

name: Request admission transaction with request series
what: Each step builds its model request as a pure function of the log: prompt reconciliation, user admission, header/context logging and freezing happen synchronously after the async route preparation, so a cancel during preparation commits nothing.
how: agent/pre-step returns reject or enter(messages, startsRequestSeries); step/start precedes agent/request and ctx.llm.prepareCall(); then the loop reconciles the system prompt against the prepared-call capability, appends user/message once, logs request/header and request/context only when changed, derives and deep-freezes the request. Retries reuse the rendered assembly and do not repeat pre-step or user admission.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane could adopt the rule that route resolution happens before any log commit, so cancellation and retry never leave half-admitted prompts or duplicate user messages.
notes: The 'series' concept (a run of requests whose prefix must stay byte-stable) is the key to the cache-aware behaviour documented in the KV-cache records.

name: Cancellation preserves the prefix the user already saw
what: When a stream is cancelled, the delivered text is recorded as an interrupted assistant message, so the follow-up and any fork see what the user read; tool calls that never dispatched are not replayed.
how: ReactLoopAgent.step catches cancellation, asks BlockAssembler.interruptedBlocks() for non-empty text/reasoning blocks and appends assistant/message with interrupted:true plus the exact embedded timed stream before step/end and the aborted turn/end. Empty prefix becomes assistant/attempt. Cancel causes are typed (AgentCancelCause) and copied into turn/end so abort stacks stay out of the log.
verevonRelevance: Verevon chat 'stop' should persist the delivered prefix as the assistant turn; otherwise follow-ups like 'expand on point two' lose context. Cheap to copy in Model Plane session assembly.
notes: Decision note rejects appending a model-visible '[interrupted by user]' marker for now; UI renders a Stopped marker from the durable flag.

name: Paired tool history is always repaired (aborted, not-started, unknown outcome)
what: After a cancel, failed step or crash, every unanswered tool call gets an explicit error result so later requests stay valid, and uncertain side effects are never retried automatically.
how: ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH for calls cancellation prevented; TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for a recorded call without result (tells the model to retry only read-only or idempotent work); TOOL_NOT_STARTED when no call record exists. ToolCallRecovery tracks unanswered requests from committed events and is shared by live failure, crash recovery and fork-seed construction. Verified in source: the same tracker runs inside the live step (agent.ts catch block appends conservative results before step/end), and synthetic results are deterministic (ids derived from cause, call id and seq; timestamps reuse the last real event). The model-visible wording tells the model to retry only read-only or idempotent work and otherwise verify external state or ask the user; the forked variant says the parent may have completed the call after the fork point.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane resume paths should emit the same three distinct synthetic results; the 'unknown outcome' wording is a reusable safety prompt for side-effecting tools.
notes: Limitation: recovery does not rewrite unanswered calls inside already-closed historical turns.

name: Durability checkpoints before model request, tool effect and next step
what: Work becomes durable before a model request, before a top-level tool can cause external effects and before the next step, so a crash resumes from stored requests, calls and results without loss.
how: session-checkpoint-policy awaits persistence flush at those points and is fail-closed: the adapter or tool body does not run until the write succeeds. Interrupted calls recover as unknown outcome; tools are advised to forward exec.callId as an idempotency key. Resume appends synthetic turn closers; there is no partial-turn continuation. Verified in source: the whole policy is an 83-line plugin with exactly three listeners. llm/stream wraps the stream so ctx.sessions.flush(session) finishes before the first chunk is requested; tools/execute flushes before the body only for top-level calls (nested calls with exec.parent reuse the durable outer call) and returns ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH if the signal aborted during the flush; agent/pre-step flushes the preceding step's batch.
verevonRelevance: Gives a concrete write-ahead discipline for Model Plane runs: log intent, then execute, then log result; exec.callId as idempotency key should be mandatory for Quarry/integration actions.
notes: Weakness: no checkpoint inside an active model attempt, so a hard crash loses transient assistant frames.

name: Fail-closed bounded parallel tool scheduler
what: Independent tool calls in one assistant message run concurrently (default 10) while side-effecting calls act as ordering barriers; results and injected context commit in model order.
how: Registry.executionMode(exec) returns parallel only when the visible definition's isConcurrencySafe(args) is exactly true (unknown/hidden/throwing = exclusive). executeToolCalls groups calls, reclassifies each before start, drains on abort, and records synthetic results for skipped calls. maxParallelToolCalls is a volatile config field. Classification is unary only.
verevonRelevance: Already adopted by Verevon (adoption plan scorecard); the useful remainder is the per-call reclassification and 'exactly true' fail-closed rule.
notes: Cannot express sibling/resource-dependent safety (two writes to different paths); those stay exclusive.

name: Retry as durable step-level recovery with always/normal modes
what: Transient model failures are retried inside the same open turn; each scheduled retry is logged before its backoff wait, and 'always' mode retries every failure until success, cancel or disposal.
how: llm-retry is a listener on the agent/request-error waterfall that appends llm/retry (id, failure, delay) then llm/retry-started and returns {kind:'retry'}. Provider-owned policy: normal = 5 retries for EMPTY_RESPONSE, RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT with 500 ms to 10 s backoff and 10% jitter; Retry-After overrides local delay when within bounds. pi-ai SDK retries are disabled so every attempt is visible.
verevonRelevance: Retry policy belongs on the provider route and must be a logged event; Verevon cost/billing should count llm/retry attempts as separate billable requests.
notes: Always mode also retries auth/quota/invalid-request failures; no cross-provider failover exists anywhere in the repo.

name: Advisory repeat-call reminder guard
what: When a model repeats the identical tool call, it receives escalating reminders (at 3, 5, 8 repeats) to change approach; the call itself is never blocked.
how: repeat-tool-reminder canonicalizes arguments by deep key sort, tracks consecutive repeats per agent on the tool chain, clears on a new user message, and fires only at exact configured counts. Subagents keep separate chains and compaction does not reset them.
verevonRelevance: Cheap loop-hygiene guard to add to Model Plane; consider a blocking tier at a high threshold, which DSH deliberately lacks.
notes: Past the highest threshold the chain goes silent; fuzzy matching rejected.

name: Cooperative tool deadlines (no registry-wide default)
what: Tools that declare timeoutMs get a deadline enforced by a wrapper that cancels via signal and returns TOOL_TIMEOUT after the tool settles; tools without a declared budget (bash, read, write, edit) have none.
how: defineTool timeoutMs is declarative only; dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy wraps tools/execute, aborts exec.signal at the deadline and waits for downstream settlement. A tool that ignores cancellation can hold the call open. bash keeps its own executor-owned BASH_TIMEOUT and moves a timed-out foreground command to background as a job. Verified in source: the wrapper derives a deadline signal, swaps it onto exec.signal for dispatch and restores the caller's signal afterwards so post-execute listeners never see an already-aborted timeout signal; it replaces the result only when timeoutOf(signal, TOOL_TIMEOUT) shows its own timer fired, so a nested outer deadline reads as an ordinary cancel; the replacement error is ToolTimeoutError with code TOOL_TIMEOUT.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should pair deadlines with hard process-range kill for sandboxed tools; DSH only gets hard kill from the subprocess provider.
notes: Moving a timed-out foreground command to a background job instead of killing it is a notable UX choice.

name: Proactive and reactive context compaction with routed thresholds
what: Old history is summarised when the request nears the model window, and a provider context-overflow error triggers one maximal compaction and a retry.
how: compaction-basic listens on agent/pre-step (pressure) and agent/request-error (CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED). Threshold = floor(min(W*0.8, W-O-B)) with B=65,536 headroom; retained tail 16% of W-O; per-route modelPolicies. Summarizer provider/model configurable, otherwise the last routed target. Misconfiguration (no pressure budget) skips proactive compaction with one warning but overflow recovery stays available.
verevonRelevance: Formula reserves output + headroom before percentage, which avoids the classic 'compact too late on large-output models' failure; adopt for Model Plane per-route policies.
notes: No corpus-backed default ratios; meter uses a 4 chars/token heuristic that underprices CJK and JSON (compaction Dev Note).

name: Compaction as a log-recorded bracket transaction
what: Compaction either completes (summary plus replacement) or leaves a detectable orphaned lock; a summary that does not shrink its source is rejected.
how: Region transaction: validate span and live lock, append compaction/start synchronously, summarise, revalidate stability (whole surface for automatic, selected span for manual), reject non-shrinking summary, append compaction/summary plus replacement user/message, then exactly one compaction/end attempt. A failed close deliberately leaves a blocking orphan; an unmatched start before a newer session/end-seed is stale evidence.
verevonRelevance: Prior analysis noted the lock-released-last idea; the new facts are shrink validation, stability revalidation and stale-lock semantics, all directly portable to Model Plane compaction.
notes: Limitation: compactRegion requires an open turn; envelopes (system, tools, prefix) and single indivisible units cannot be compacted.

name: Warm-prefix summarizer request
what: The compaction summary call replays the conversation's own system prompt, tool declarations and shadowed messages byte-for-byte so only the final instruction and the summary output miss the provider cache.
how: summarize() sends the surface node-0 system message, the last routed request's tools (with toolHistory projection) and the shadowed region, then appends a frozen RequestUserInput instruction with a eight-section structured checkpoint template (primary request, key concepts, files, errors, pending, current work, next step, critical context); only text is kept and wrapped in compacted-summary tags. Request carries purpose 'compaction' which the DeepSeek adapter turns into header x-deepseek-harness-compact: 1. Verified in source: the template has eight sections (Primary Request and Intent, Key Technical Concepts, Files and Code, Errors and Fixes, Pending Jobs, Current Work, Next Step, Critical Context). A prior compacted-summary block inside the conversation is merged into one consolidated checkpoint instead of being copied forward, the output is wrapped with a fixed preamble that tells the model to continue without acknowledging the checkpoint, image output and max-tokens truncation fail closed, and the summarizer target defaults to the last routed provider and model.
verevonRelevance: Highest-value copy for cost: Model Plane compaction should reuse the live prefix and put the instruction last, and tag the call so providers/billing see it as compaction.
notes: The pass-2 Verevon adoption plan says cache-aware compaction is 'largely already true'; this record documents the concrete byte-for-byte mechanism to verify against.

name: Two-stage reduction: model-free tool-result pruning before summarisation
what: Oversized tool results are first trimmed to head, a middle-pruned marker and tail without any model call, and summarisation is skipped when that is enough.
how: compaction-tool-result-pruner runs only after a compaction trigger qualifies (below pressure nothing is touched). Defaults: threshold 8,192 code points, keep 4,096 head and 1,024 tail. Replacement cites the original event via sourceEventSeqs; compaction/prune carries a shadow price so projections subtract it without per-node state. Verified in source: measurement and slicing are by Unicode code point (a surrogate pair is never split), non-text blocks are kept in order, the replacement must be smaller than both the original and the threshold or the pass throws, and the 'compaction/prune' shadow-price event is appended synchronously immediately before each replacement with shadowedTokenCount from tokenMeter.estimateMessage. Shipped config: thresholdChars 8192, headChars 4096, tailChars 1024.
verevonRelevance: A model-free first tier is cheap to add and keeps originals replayable; Model Plane should log replacements with source references rather than mutating tool outputs.
notes: Pruning is syntactic (head/tail), not semantic.

name: Image offload on route rejection
what: When an image-capable route rejects a request over its image budget, the oldest images are replaced by placeholders naming attachment and path, logged once, and the request is retried without spending retry budget.
how: Adapters fail with IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED naming how many more oldest occurrences must go; compaction-image-offload logs one image/offload event; later requests keep the choice across route change, resume and replay. Files-mode and inline-mode removal use byte/count quanta (64 MiB / 10 MiB / 20 images) to avoid rewriting the prefix after every new image.
verevonRelevance: Stepped high-watermark removal is a neat cache-aware trick for image-heavy chat; offloaded images never return automatically, a deliberate trade-off.
notes: Every offload costs a failed request; planned move to provider-reported uncacheable images.

name: Oversized tool output spill to private files
what: Long tool output is replaced by ordered head/tail content within a shared token budget plus a path to the full result the model can read or grep; images stay in attachment storage.
how: spill-policy (maxInlineTokens 12,500 in base) calls ctx.spillStore, which saves text to a per-session private 0700 directory with random names and exclusive 0600 opens and returns an opaque locator and retrieval guidance. Recovery failure leaves the original inline. Locators need a co-located filesystem consumer; no retrieval or deletion API. Spill-file writing in the subprocess collector is best-effort at every step: a filesystem failure while opening or appending discards the spill, reports once through the owner's logger and leaves the in-memory tail collecting; the removed private spill directory is deliberately not recreated because the design rests on a random name created once by the process (decision note 2026-09-22).
verevonRelevance: Same pattern Claude Code and Codex use; DSH's private-directory hardening and spill-notice convention are worth copying for Model Plane sandboxes.
notes: Spill files are never deleted until restart sweep; storage is not access control.

name: Replay-deterministic token meter
what: Context pressure, token usage and per-category breakdown are computed by folding the session log, so compaction, UI meters and telemetry share one deterministic number.
how: ctx.tokenMeter folds consumed-log revisions into a priced surface; provider usage anchors a measurement only when the canonical request envelope is identical and total is at least the route-priced cost; otherwise a 4-chars-per-token heuristic plus overhead is used. Image occurrences use adapter-declared visual-token pricing; files are priced as handle text. Exposed through session projections tokenUsage, contextPressure, contextBreakdown. Verified in source: the heuristic is ceil(chars/4) plus 4 per block and 4 per role frame, tool schemas price as JSON length/4, usage buckets are summed disjoint (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite + output) and a mismatch between asked and answered image-price counts throws rather than mispricing.
verevonRelevance: A single log-folding meter avoids drift between compaction triggers and UI occupancy; Model Plane cost plane could reuse the same fold for billing reconciliation.
notes: No currency cost anywhere; heuristic not tokenizer-exact.

name: Durable clock readings as appended context
what: The model gets the current time, the browser zone and elapsed time since the previous message as durable sourced context rather than a mutable system-prompt line.
how: dsh-time-context appends a source-attributed reading on eligible steps (default minimum interval 10 minutes, 0 = every step); mixed browser zones make the model ask. Declared by standard/cordis/ptc presets, absent from the Web default row.
verevonRelevance: Time/zone belongs in appended context, not the system prompt, to keep the cached prefix stable; relevant to Verevon workspaces with multi-timezone users.
notes: History cost accumulates between compactions.

name: Workspace instruction chain with byte budget and touch-driven refresh
what: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md files from user-global and project scopes are loaded once and refreshed when file tools touch nested directories, with broader files dropped before the most specific is truncated.
how: dsh-agent-instructions builds a chain (maxBytes 65,536), supports AGENTS.local.md overlays and a shared ~/.agents root, deduplicates byte-identical candidates, and reconciles on resume. No watcher: refresh happens on successful read/write/edit. Symlinked instruction files are followed (documented trust gap). Verified in source: baseline instructions enter durable context before the first request, successful fs tool touches project nested, changed and removed instruction files into the inbox, content-identical candidates are dropped, truncation leaves a notice that instructions were omitted or truncated to fit the budget, and the rendered text says more specific instructions take precedence.
verevonRelevance: Verevon knowledge/instruction layers could use the same budgeted chain; watch the symlink trust boundary for untrusted repos.
notes: Shell navigation does not trigger nested discovery.

name: Unified subagent activation API (local conversations and external executions)
what: One service starts delegated work through named providers: in-process spawn and fork children keep durable sessions and accept messages; ACP, DSH SDK, Codex and Claude Code run once and return final text.
how: startActivation(spec) with capability flags (agentOptions, outputSchema, depthLimit, toolFilter, persona) validated before start; delivery 'parent' notifies the model, 'caller' only returns the result to workflow/PTC consumers. Local children enter the parent catalog; descriptors persist so cold resume works. Requests needing unsupported options are rejected, not ignored.
verevonRelevance: A capability-flag handshake per sandbox/agent backend is a clean way for Model Plane to unify internal agents with remote agents (A2A/ACP) without silent option loss.
notes: Process-local residency only; no durable parent mailbox; accepted-but-unlogged messages are lost on crash.

name: Cache-preserving fork subagent
what: A forked child sees the parent's completed turns and keeps the parent's provider/model so the copied history stays eligible for prefix-cache reuse.
how: subagent-fork-in-process seeds the child with a balanced completed-turn prefix (buildForkSeed, inherited marker, closers with reason 'forked'); the shipped subagent_fork tool deliberately omits route selection, and parent and child messaging tool definitions match byte for byte.
verevonRelevance: Fork-with-shared-prefix is a cost lever for Verevon parallel research/agent fan-out; Model Plane should pin route and tool definitions for fork children.
notes: Explicit persona, tool filter, SDK or route changes break equality and forfeit reuse.

name: Persisted delegation depth and per-preset child tool denial
what: Subagents cannot recurse past a depth cap or use reminder tools, and the depth survives cold resume.
how: resolveChildDepth reads the persisted session header delegationDepth against maxDepth; tool-subagent rows in presets carry toolFilter.deny for schedule_*; schedule and ask_user refuse live delegated callers (DELEGATED_CALLER / subagent_session).
verevonRelevance: Persisting depth in the session header is the robust way to enforce delegation caps across restarts; also model that children cannot ask the user.

name: Structured subagent results through a terminal tool
what: A caller-supplied JSON schema makes the child report its final answer by calling a reserved structured_output tool; the value is captured only after the authoritative tool result succeeds.
how: attachStructuredRuntime registers a child-scoped tool, a trailing prompt instruction and a monotonic guard so no later calls reopen the completed run; capture also waits for the enclosing run_code in PTC mode. Schemas must be object-rooted at the subagent/workflow layer. No response_format is used.
verevonRelevance: Terminal-tool structured output works on every provider (no response_format dependency); Model Plane should prefer it for multi-provider agent results.

name: Other agent products as one-shot subagent backends
what: A delegated task can run as an unattended Claude Code session, a Codex thread, an ACP-compatible agent or a child DSH runtime, returning only final text.
how: subagent-claude-code (Claude Agent SDK, one query per run), subagent-codex (Codex app-server pinned to 0.153.4 protocol), subagent-acp (fresh subprocess, stdin-EOF-first teardown), subagent-dsh-sdk (child runtime over JSON-RPC). Permission prompts are auto-denied/auto-answered by policy; tool traffic, reasoning, stderr and workspace diffs stay outside the parent session.
verevonRelevance: Interop pattern for Verevon: treat third-party coding agents as sandboxed one-shot workers behind the same activation contract; remember they bypass Verevon's ZDR and audit unless contained.
notes: Heavy per-run spawn cost; no pooling; no timeout or side-effect rollback.

name: Owner-scoped background jobs with completion notices and wake budget
what: Long commands and workflows run as jobs owned by the starting agent; completion arrives as an in-session notice that wakes an idle owner, bounded by an optional consecutive-wake budget.
how: ctx.jobs registry assigns <kind>-N ids, fences reads/cancels by owner session, keeps retained output with a model-only consuming cursor and a non-consuming readAt for UIs; tool-jobs injects notices (next step if busy, waking message if idle). bash/pwsh register every command as a job from start; a foreground command exceeding its timeout returns the same job id. Verified in source (service contract): settlement is first-wins with one terminal record, and the 'settled' event reports whether a waiter already collected it ('awaited') so completion reporters can skip it; start() refuses work while no attached job controller serves the owner; each job has one bounded output ring with a model consuming cursor and absolute-offset observers, a reader below the retained window gets a lossy read rather than an error, and settlement trims retention to a settled cap; owner or service disposal cancels live work and a throwing cancel force-fails only the record with cause 'teardown'.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane background runs already exist; the wake budget and non-consuming UI read are small additions worth copying.
notes: Jobs are process-local and die with the process.

name: Durable host-level scheduled reminders
what: The agent (or user) creates one-shot, interval, daily, weekly or cron reminders that are delivered as follow-up messages to the original session and restore a cold session when due.
how: dsh-schedule stores tasks in a storage domain, keeps only the latest missed occurrence per recurring task, resolves IANA zones, five-field Vixie cron (no seconds, names or macros), prunes delivery history, and refuses delegated subagent callers. Delivery is at-least-once; enqueue and task writes are not atomic. Needs the Host running. Verified in source: minimum fixed-rate interval is 60 s, the cron date search is bounded to 400 years so an unsatisfiable rule has fixed creation cost, and delivery restores the owning session through sessionController.resolveAgent, calls agent.followup with a user message of source kind 'schedule' whose text is a fixed '[SCHEDULE REMINDER]' frame with JSON-escaped schedule id, occurrence time and prompt (so a stored prompt cannot forge framing), requires ctx.sessions.flush to acknowledge, and only then commits the delivery record. Recurring tasks of one session are batched into a single message, a wall-clock rollback during restoration re-filters members that are no longer due, and delivery history is pruned to 30 days or 200 records per task by default.
verevonRelevance: Verevon automations need server-side scheduling with idempotent delivery; DSH shows the minimum viable semantics and its at-least-once gap.
notes: Desktop does not enable scheduled tasks by default; no pause state.

name: Durable same-session goals with a round-driver
what: A user or agent sets one persistent objective that survives resume and fork; an idle agent is re-prompted for further rounds until it records completion or a blocker or the round cap (256) is hit.
how: dsh-goal stores goal/change events with compare-and-set updates and stable blocker codes; goal-round-driver continues while idle and armed; tool-goal defines when repeated blocking stops continuation. Continuation permission is process-local. No independent evaluator, no token/time budget.
verevonRelevance: A durable goal object with CAS updates is a clean primitive for Verevon long-running agent tasks; add a cost/time budget and evaluator, which DSH lacks.
notes: Completion is authoritative from the same model that is working.

name: Plan mode is guidance only; tool catalog stays fixed for cache stability
what: Plan mode changes behaviour through prompt text and a reviewed exit_plan_mode, while every tool stays declared so the request prefix does not change between modes.
how: plan-mode contributes a section (in the shipped base config) that tells the model mutation tools stay listed only to keep the request shape stable; the plan is submitted as the sole final tool call, which concludes the turn and opens a plan-review interaction. Enforcement must come from sandbox mode and approval policy configured separately.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon adds plan mode, copy the cache-stable tool list and enforce read-only separately in the sandbox/permission layer; text-only plan mode is bypassable.

name: Programmable workflows in a sandboxed Node child
what: For explicit multi-agent orchestration the model writes JavaScript that fans work to subagents with agent(), parallel(), pipeline(), phase() and log() and returns one JSON value.
how: workflow-ptc runs the script in a fresh Node PTC process under the session sandbox policy, reusing the PTC provider; children are attributed to the caller; foreground runs await all work, background runs return a job id. No journaling/resume, no saved or nested workflows, caps are cooperative counters, the VM is not a security boundary.
verevonRelevance: Code-as-orchestration is a flexible alternative to a fixed DAG engine; Verevon should journal runs (DSH does not) if it copies this.
notes: A restart cannot continue a run.

name: Ralph-style fresh-context rounds (experimental)
what: A foreground loop runs fresh child agents against one immutable objective, passing only a bounded report and the workspace between rounds.
how: tool-ralph on the workflow engine; each round is one fresh child with no parent or prior transcript; stops on worker-declared completion, blocker or round limit; failures of a child end the run without retry. Completion is self-declared; recursion denial is not enforced.
verevonRelevance: Fresh-context loops limit context rot for long coding tasks; needs an external verifier before Verevon relies on it.
notes: Experimental, ships off.

name: Agent Teams with durable task board (experimental)
what: A lead can spawn named teammates, message them directly and share a durable task list with owners and dependencies.
how: dsh-experimental-agent-team keeps roster and task state; sends use target inbox and cold-resume stored teammates; tools spawn_teammate, team_task_*, wait_agent, send_message. One shared checkout with advisory write scopes; no worktree, locks or automatic ownership release; whole-view broadcasts to every connected browser. Verified in source: the board is a small state machine over durable events in the Lead's log (pending to in_progress to completed, with release, reopen and reassign); only the owner or the Lead may mutate a task (TEAM_TASK_UNAUTHORIZED), claiming requires the task to be pending and ready (all blockers complete), and every candidate snapshot is validated against the whole active dependency graph for missing, duplicate, self-referential and cyclic blockers before the event is appended.
verevonRelevance: Useful reference for Verevon multi-agent boards, but note the shared-checkout and broadcast limits.
notes: Prototype with no stability promise.

name: Timed user questions with two settlements
what: A question can release the model after a timeout to continue independent work while it stays answerable; the late answer arrives as a new input.
how: ask_user_question in blocking mode or mode:timed (timeout -1 = wait forever); ctx.userQuestions.askTimed returns a first settlement (answered or timed out) and keeps the question in a projection across restarts and clients. Live subagent children cannot ask.
verevonRelevance: Non-blocking human-in-the-loop questions fit Verevon approvals/clarifications that must not stall unattended runs.

name: Maintenance tasks and awaited agent-creation transaction
what: Hosts can run non-turn maintenance (compaction) from the true idle phase, and agent creation is one rollback-covered transaction.
how: Agent.runMaintenance(task) claims the idle phase, keeps public status idle and holds later waking input in the inbox until done. ctx.agents.create builds session, agent and scoped context, awaits setup, enters registries, announces session/created, awaits serial agent/created listeners, then releases queued input; failure rolls back everything.
verevonRelevance: The creation-transaction discipline (rollback on listener failure) prevents half-initialised agents; relevant for Model Plane agent spawn paths.

name: Webhook-to-session ingress (experimental)
what: A trusted rule turns an external event (for example a signed GitHub delivery) into a new root session in a workspace, enabling review bots.
how: ctx.webhookRuntime.register(rule) / dispatch(delivery); webhook-github adds Octokit signature verification on ctx.webServer. Process-local fire-and-forget; no queue, retry, deduplication or completion result.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the durable, idempotent version of this (queue + dedup + result) in Model Plane triggers.
notes: Marked experimental.

name: Twin LLM adapters: native DeepSeek Messages plus pi-ai multi-provider
what: The harness ships two structurally different adapters behind one service: a first-party DeepSeek Messages transport and a pi-ai-backed adapter that routes to other providers, gateways and self-hosted servers.
how: dsh-llm-deepseek (routes deepseek-official, deepseek-account) and dsh-llm-pi-ai (provider profiles in settings) register disjoint route names on ctx.llm; pi-ai is mounted dormant with zero routes until a llm-pi-ai settings section adds profiles. Registering a duplicate route fails with DUPLICATE_ADAPTER. Adapters own wire format; the service owns the neutral message/content-block/stream vocabulary.
verevonRelevance: Keeps vendor-specific optimisations (cache protocol, Files API, thinking signatures) in a first-party adapter without forcing them into the neutral vocabulary; Model Plane could do the same per provider crate.
notes: Cost: two adapters mean cache-update capabilities exist only where the pi-ai catalog flags them (pi-ai declares no tool-update mode).

name: Capability-resolved model metadata and one-shot prepared calls
what: Before any provider I/O the harness resolves the exact model's context window, output default, reasoning efforts, input modalities and update modes, validates the call config against them and binds everything to the adapter generation that will dispatch.
how: ctx.llm.prepareCall(config, signal, configure?) takes a pure ConfigureCall over detached frozen controls and model metadata, materialises adapter defaults, validates reasoning effort, and returns a frozen one-shot call; dispatch must match the prepared config. HMR or dynamic settings cannot mix one generation's image capability with another's endpoint. Provider/model/effort are volatile config fields applied to the next call.
verevonRelevance: A resolved, validated, frozen call object is a good seam for Model Plane inference routing: capability checks happen before spend, and hot config changes cannot split a request across generations.

name: KV-cache-aware system-prompt updates (in-history mode)
what: When a model reads the latest system message at any position, a changed prompt is appended after the cached history instead of rewriting the first message, so the provider prefix cache survives prompt changes within a request series.
how: LlmResolvedModelInfo.systemPromptUpdate = 'in-history' (declared per model, default deepseek-flash). The loop appends a non-empty changed prompt as a later system/message inside a continuing series; incapable routes and new series consolidate at the first system node with logged per-node empty replacements. DeepSeek serialization keeps the initial top-level system and sends later snapshots after their corresponding user/tool-result turn; invalid placement fails with UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT.
verevonRelevance: Dynamic system prompts (per-workspace rules, skills, time) usually destroy cache; this append-only protocol is a model-API feature Verevon should request or emulate with appended developer messages.
notes: Requires provider support (DeepSeek beta behaviour); only DeepSeek and flagged pi-ai catalog models get it.

name: Mid-conversation tool changes with deferred loading
what: Tools added during a conversation (plugin or MCP) are announced by a developer message and a deferred declaration rather than rewriting the cached tool list; removals can stay declared.
how: request/header.tools records active tools; a diff against the previous header emits one developer/message with tool-addition/tool-removal blocks (additions reference the new header through headerSeq). Session.toolHistory() folds headers and updates; at dispatch projectToolUpdates uses the route's toolUpdate mode ('addition-only' or 'in-history'). DeepSeek sends system-role tool_addition/tool_removal blocks, defer_loading on declarations and beta header mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01. Changed same-name schemas still rebuild declarations and lose cache.
verevonRelevance: Directly relevant to Verevon connectors/MCP: adding an integration mid-chat should not invalidate the whole prefix; Model Plane should record tool sets in a header and diff them.
notes: Registration-time check for incompatible same-name schema changes is deferred.

name: Reasoning effort and thinking controls
what: Each model advertises ordered reasoning efforts (off, low, high, max); the chosen value is validated against that exact model before any network I/O and mapped to the provider's wire field.
how: DeepSeek: low/high/max enable thinking and serialise as output_config.effort; off sends thinking.type disabled; thinking: disabled in deployment config locks every request to off; unsupported values fail with UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT. pi-ai profiles remap level names (reasoningEfforts map) and expose compat switches (thinkingFormat deepseek, thinkingTokenBudgetField). Reasoning tokens count toward the output cap.
verevonRelevance: Per-model effort lists with selection guidance are the clean way to drive a Verevon effort picker without hard-coding provider names.
notes: Selecting off does not guarantee disabled reasoning on protocols that express it by omission.

name: Replay state and thinking signatures are validated and not portable across models
what: Assistant thinking signatures and response metadata are replayed only to the same adapter and model; invalid or cross-model state is dropped with a warning while text and tool history stay intact.
how: Each assistant message carries a ReplayEnvelope (response + per-block metadata). llm-deepseek readReplay validates kind/version/model/block types and signature placement and returns undefined (degraded) for foreign, cross-model or malformed history; the runtime drops replay state unless the same adapter instance owns both routes.
verevonRelevance: Mid-chat model switching (a Verevon chat feature) needs exactly this rule: strip provider-private thinking metadata when the route changes.

name: DeepSeek Files API image pipeline with upload cache
what: Images are normalised to the provider's vision grid, uploaded once through /v1/files and referenced by file id, with inline base64 only as a whole-request fallback.
how: Target size follows 14px patches, 3:1 downsampling, max 1024 tokens (square 1302x1302, 16:9 1708x961), 4096 px cap, 2 MiB default; alpha as WebP effort 0, opaque as JPEG on 85/75/60 ladder. file-store caches ids per endpoint plus credential-header hash with singleflight, refresh margin, stale-file invalidation and oldest-first quota cleanup (batch 100); a request never mixes file ids and inline images. Every image is preceded by text naming attachment id and request dimensions.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon vision uploads, deterministic per-route request versions plus content-addressed upload caching cut both tokens and bytes; copy the stable-prefix property (same bytes every request).
notes: Assistant image output is unsupported; images are input-only.

name: Files never reach providers: deterministic handle text instead
what: Uploaded non-image files are not sent natively; every occurrence becomes one stable line naming the file, size and read-only saved path, and the model reads it with file tools on demand.
how: FileBlock is a durable verbatim reference; request assembly replaces each occurrence (including tool-result occurrences) with deterministic handle text resolved through attachment and filesystem providers; ctx.llm.fileRequestText exposes the projection for measurement. Text-only routes get per-image placeholders without rewriting append-only history.
verevonRelevance: A uniform 'handle line + tool read' rule avoids provider file-API divergence and keeps prefixes stable; fits Verevon documents from the Data Plane being passed as references.
notes: No native PDF/audio/video handling; the model must read via tools.

name: Disjoint token usage accounting with cache read/write and reasoning tokens
what: Every call reports uncached input, output, cache-read, cache-write and reasoning tokens as disjoint counts so billed input equals their sum.
how: TokenUsage {inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens?, cacheReadTokens?, cacheWriteTokens?, reasoningTokens?}; adapters whose providers fold cache hits into prompt_tokens (DeepSeek) subtract them out; usage must precede the terminal finish chunk. UI shows cache counts per turn (scout inventory).
verevonRelevance: Adopt the disjoint-count convention in Model Plane cost records so cache savings are visible and reconcilable; currency pricing is still missing in DSH.
notes: No currency price tables anywhere in the repo (SRC keyword check).

name: Purpose-tagged auxiliary model calls and model-hidden request metadata
what: Compaction and session-title calls are tagged so adapters can attach transport metadata (headers) without altering model input.
how: GenerateOptions.purpose 'compaction' | 'session-title' and sessionId; DeepSeek adapter adds x-deepseek-harness-user-id (anonymous UUID), x-deepseek-harness-session-id and x-deepseek-harness-compact headers; credential failure happens before identity resolution so unauthorised requests send nothing. Search auxiliary calls record their exact secret-free request before dispatch and a recorder throw blocks dispatch.
verevonRelevance: Verevon billing and ZDR enforcement need the same per-purpose tagging on every inference call so auxiliary calls are attributable and policy-checked.
notes: The same headers are an identity/telemetry channel to the provider (see safety records).

name: Native server-side web search through the Anthropic-compatible web_search tool
what: web_search is a full auxiliary model request that uses the endpoint's built-in web_search_20250305 server tool and returns structured result blocks with cited snippets.
how: web-search-deepseek posts to /anthropic/v1/messages with maxUses (default 5) and parses web_search_result items plus citations[] into a url-to-cited-text snippet map; absence of structured blocks is an error, not a prose-scraping fallback. Exa and Perplexity providers are alternatives selected by DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER. Seam facts verified in source: every search backend is normalized to WebSearchResult {content?, sources[{url, title?, snippet?, publishedAt?}], truncated} and the seam itself cuts sources to maxResults when a provider cannot limit them; providers register by id with a cheap local available() check; a non-2xx fetch is a result (status is data) while WebError is reserved for unsafe or unrepresentable resources; WebFetchBody is a closed html|text union so a new kind breaks compilation at every consumer.
verevonRelevance: Provider-native search keeps citations structured, but it costs a model turn per search; Verevon Research should decide per provider whether native search or Quarry-backed search is cheaper and ZDR-safe.
notes: No batch-wide search counter: maxUses multiplies by searchMaxQueries.

name: Deliberately minimal sampling vocabulary (no tool_choice, no response_format)
what: The neutral request carries temperature, maxTokens and stop only; tool_choice, top_p, penalties and JSON-mode are not mapped, and structured results use a terminal tool instead.
how: GenerateOptions has no tool_choice or response_format; llm-deepseek states tool_choice is not mapped; llm-pi-ai rejects stop with UNSUPPORTED_OPTION; producer-less vocabulary (prefill, strict, cache hints) was pruned. Streamed tool arguments remain raw JSON strings until block-end.
verevonRelevance: A gap against OpenAI/Anthropic-grade routing: Model Plane should keep tool_choice/response_format in its neutral vocabulary because Verevon needs forced tools and schema-constrained outputs.
notes: Drop-inert-knobs policy is a process choice: vocabulary grows only when a producer exists.

name: Custom provider routes: three protocols, compat switches and endpoint model discovery
what: Users can add third-party providers from the pi-ai catalog or declare a gateway with openai-completions, openai-responses or anthropic-messages, and discover its models from the endpoint.
how: llm-pi-ai profiles (providers dictionary) with api/baseURL/models/modelOverrides/compat; modelOverrides reshape catalog models without replacing the list and refuse typos; discovery uses GET /models (OpenAI shapes) or /v1/models?limit=1000 (Anthropic) and returns candidates only; vllmPriority and thinkingTokenBudgetField for self-hosted servers; one protocol per route.
verevonRelevance: Comparable to Verevon BYO-model needs; note the rule that discovery never mutates config and that a modality declaration is unverified until the provider rejects it.
notes: No Ollama/LM Studio providers; keyless local servers need a placeholder credential.

name: pi-ai OAuth and interactive-key sign-in exist in code; docs are stale
what: The pi-ai adapter exposes OAuth or interactive-key login for catalog providers through the authorization seam, except OpenAI, whose account sign-in needs an installation id the harness lacks.
how: login.ts builds loginMethods per provider (oauth via provider.auth.oauth unless in UNSERVED_OAUTH = {openai}; api-key only when the provider collects it interactively); stored credentials live at llm-pi-ai/<provider id> with cross-process refresh locking; a sign-in is process-local and abandoned on reload. docs/user/guide/providers.md still says OAuth providers such as Codex are not supported in the Web form.
verevonRelevance: Resolves the scout's doc/code conflict in favour of code; whether the Web Models page surfaces the OAuth method was not verified. Relevant to Verevon BYO subscription logins (OAuth flows must be durable, unlike here).
notes: Attempts are not resumable and sign-out does not revoke at the issuer.

name: DeepSeek V4 route catalog facts and stream idle timeout
what: The default DeepSeek route advertises a text+image deepseek-flash and text-only deepseek-v4-pro, each with a 1,000,000-token window, a 256,000 default output cap and a 300 s idle-read deadline.
how: llm-deepseek config: baseURL https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic, defaultContextWindow 1,000,000, maxTokens 256,000, streamIdleTimeoutMs 300,000, models catalog advisory (core passes unlisted ids through as text-only), per-entry imagePixelBudget/imageMaxBytes/systemPromptUpdate/toolUpdate. Catalog is not validated against the gateway.
verevonRelevance: Useful calibration for 1M-window planning (headroom 65,536 means compaction triggers at 0.8 x 1M); not directly Verevon-specific.
notes: Catalog requests can fail with INVALID_REQUEST until the gateway enables the id.

name: Argument-order engineering for streaming tool calls
what: Tool schemas list a human-readable description before the command or code, and a prompt sentence reinforces the order, so UIs can show intent while arguments still stream.
how: A 310-request measurement on DeepSeek V4 showed reordering properties alone failed; reordering required plus an explicit instruction made free-calling Flash put description first 19/20 and Pro 20/20 for bash, 20/20 for run_code. The defineTool schema DSL emits required in declaration order, so source order controls it; tool descriptions carry the sentence Provide description before command.
verevonRelevance: Cheap, measured trick for Verevon agent pages that stream tool intent; test the same ordering on each Model Plane provider before relying on it.
notes: Measured with a minimal system prompt, not the full harness prompt (note's own caveat).

name: Everything-is-a-plugin substrate (Cordis): services, typed events, reversible effects
what: Model adapter, tool registry, session log, agent loop, sandbox and UI are all plugins mounted on one context; every registration is an effect that unwinds on unload, enabling hot swap and per-agent scoping.
how: Plugins declare inject; services claim ctx.<key>; typed events use declaration merging with five dispatch modes (emit, waterfall, parallel, serial, bail); ctx.effect()/ctx.on() return disposers; Fibers have a lifecycle (pending, loading, active, unloading) with local hardening patches. Loader instantiates plugin trees from YAML.
verevonRelevance: The pattern (services by key, reversible effects, waterfall middleware) maps to Rust trait objects + RAII guards; Model Plane need not copy the DI framework but should keep the 'registration returns a disposer' rule.
notes: Concentrates risk in one upstream framework (vendored with 23 local modifications).

name: Capability seams: Service Definition, Provider and Consumer roles
what: Each swappable capability (llm, fs, shell, subprocess, sandbox, web, lsp, jobs, terminals, browser-use, computer-use, speech) is designed as three roles, so one provider swap changes the whole product.
how: A seam is complete only with all three roles; extension plugins depend on Service Definitions, never concrete providers; docs/capability-seams.md is a generated graph of owners, implementations and consumers. fs + subprocess define one execution world shared by Bash, PTY and LSP.
verevonRelevance: A written seam rule (definition/provider/consumer) is a good checklist for Model Plane plane boundaries and for Verevon's 'Model proposes, Quarry executes' split.
notes: Seam inventory is generated (gen-doc-graphs) and freshness-gated in CI.

name: Layered profile/bundle/patch composition with dump-config
what: A running instance is a plugin tree composed from ordered bundles, the user's profile patch, a home patch and command-line overlays; the user can print the exact composed tree.
how: Profile = ordered bundles + cordis.patch.yml; patches target a row by id and replace its whole config or insert rows; !!js expressions allowed only under plugin config and disabled; dsh --dump-config reuses the exported applyEntryPatches so config tooling never reimplements the algorithm; --dump-config-schema emits JSON Schema. Shipped profiles web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp (+desktop).
verevonRelevance: Declarative, inspectable composition is the strongest transparency lever; Model Plane agent definitions could be 'rows with ids' that tenants override, with a dump command for support.
notes: Whole-config replacement (no deep merge) makes overrides restate fields; eager non-transactional tree mutation can leave partial state on activation failure.

name: Per-session agent presets as plugin subtrees with isolation realms
what: Each session mounts a preset (standard, ptc, minimal, cordis creator) that composes that agent's tools, prompt sections, skills and delegation backends; the Web editor saves edits as profile patches.
how: The Web overlay disables the agent-plane rows on the host and inserts agent-preset declarations (cordis:group with isolate realms such as planMode, compaction, workflowEngine, terminals); host-plane services that other rows read (jobs registry, goals, token meter, subagent registry, skill registry) stay global. default: standard. minimal = persistent-shell-only agent with a complete custom persona and no runtime context.
verevonRelevance: Per-session capability sets are how Verevon could offer role-based agents (research, coding, support) with different tools and ZDR/permission posture while sharing one runtime.
notes: Presets are not security boundaries; plugin code runs with Host authority.

name: Typed tool definition DSL with SDK projections
what: Tool authors declare typed parameters, outputs, timeouts, parallel-safety, deferred loading and UI presenters once; schemas project to JSON Schema, TypeScript declarations and Python stubs.
how: defineTool (schema.ts) builds a ToolDefinition with parameterSchemaSpec to JSON Schema (required emitted in declaration order), isConcurrencySafe(args), timeoutMs, deferLoading, projectContent/finalizeContent hooks and pure presentCall/presentResult; ts-types.ts and py-types.ts generate the SDK text used by PTC mode. Arguments and results are lossless-JSON validated; ToolArgsError becomes a model-visible error without ending the turn.
verevonRelevance: A single declarative definition that yields prompt schema, SDK text and UI presenter is worth copying for Model Plane tool registration (derive from Rust types).

name: Five-stage guarded tool pipeline with monotonic guards and approval ask
what: Every call passes pre-execute policy (allow/deny/ask), deny-only monotonic guards, around-dispatch wrappers, post-execute accept/block/replace, content finalisation and a frozen result notification before tool/result is logged.
how: tools/pre-execute waterfall (permission, sandbox, hooks) may return ask, which ctx.approval resolves before guards; ctx.tools.guard() guards are checked global then scope chain farthest-first and cannot force-allow; tools/execute wraps dispatch (timeout, metrics); projectContent installs prepared content; tools/post-execute may replace, block or add context; finalizeContent enforces a content-only invariant; tools/result observes the immutable lossless-JSON outcome; failures normalise to isError results. pre-execute cannot rewrite arguments (rewrite design is a proposed note).
verevonRelevance: The ordered-policy plus unforgeable-deny split is the right shape for Model Plane's capability/hook/permission pipeline; prior analysis flagged only the guard split, the finalisation and ask stages are additional.
notes: Argument rewriting (Claude Code updatedInput) is unsupported because history and audit would desync.

name: PTC mode: the model calls tools by writing a TypeScript or Python program
what: In ptc presentation the model sees one run_code tool plus a generated SDK in the prompt; the program calls tools as await tools.name(args) and returns only curated output.
how: Registry collapses the surface to run_code (other direct calls resolve to UNKNOWN_TOOL); sub-calls re-enter the full guarded pipeline, run under a per-run pool reusing native concurrency rules and log tool/ptc-dispatch-start and tool/ptc-dispatch with ids <parent>:ptc:<n>; image results are appended as ptc-mode context. Programs run in a fresh Node process (V8 heap cap 512 MB, 120 s default, 64 MiB output) under the session sandbox with an empty process.env; wider sandbox needs justification + approval; no state persists between runs; an experimental Python provider exists.
verevonRelevance: A programmatic-tool-calling mode reduces round trips and tokens for data tasks; Model Plane could offer it behind a Quarry/sandbox executor, keeping sub-call audit events.
notes: Intermediate values are not replayable from the log and are unbounded by bytes; one language per deployment.

name: MCP client with scoped servers, durable image bridge and resource tools
what: External MCP servers (stdio or Streamable HTTP) expose tools as mcp__<server>__<tool>, server instructions join the prompt, and shared resource tools read documents on demand.
how: mcp-client attaches servers per scope (empty scope adds no tools or prompt text), uses a configured reconnect budget, bridges only PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF results into durable context (audio/embedded resources stay execution-local), rejects task-required tools; mcp-resources adds list_mcp_resources, list_mcp_resource_templates, read_mcp_resource with an explicit server name. No prompts, subscriptions or task extension. Verified in source: the public name is mcp__<serverName>__<rawName> limited to 64 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_-] with a 12-hex SHA-256 identity suffix whenever normalization or truncation changes it (the raw name is only sent on the wire and never recovered by parsing the public name); a tool-list refresh builds the whole next generation first and swaps only on success; serverName must match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32} and is reserved per registration scope; reconnect defaults are on, 500 ms to 30 s backoff, 10 attempts; attributed server instructions are capped at 32 KiB; stdio servers start with the scrubbed parent environment.
verevonRelevance: Per-scope MCP attachment fits Verevon Spaces; note the lack of MCP prompts/sampling/elicitation and that a missing capability still lists tools.
notes: MCP SDK default 60 s startup/discovery timeout is not separately configurable.

name: Skills catalog: SKILL.md bundles, durable catalog message and on-demand body load
what: Skills are directories with SKILL.md (or flat .md) discovered from project, custom, user and bundled roots; the model sees a capped catalog and loads full instructions with the skill tool, and users invoke /name.
how: skill-filesystem scans one level deep with chokidar watch; the registry resolves duplicate names first-wins by layer; tool-skill appends a durable catalog on first request and a whole-list replacement when names/descriptions change; bodies are ordinary tool history, uncapped and unversioned. Office and Windows-ACL-diagnosis skills ship bundled. Verified in source (registry): names must be kebab-case; duplicate names are resolved by explicit numeric provider rank (lower wins, bundled 600, runtime 250) before registration order; each skill carries an invocation policy {modelInvocable, userInvocable}, a source bucket (project-dsh, project-agents, runtime, user-dsh, user-agents, custom, bundled) and a resource base (directory, url or opaque) so loaded bodies can resolve relative files.
verevonRelevance: Skill format is the Claude/Codex-compatible SKILL.md, so Verevon can import those bundles; add body size caps and versioning which DSH lacks.
notes: Catalog replacement costs tokens proportional to the whole catalog on any change.

name: Transactional plugin manager with HMR and guided install
what: Users or the Creator agent can enable, disable, install and remove external plugin bundles against the active profile; installs roll back package files on failure and changes apply live when HMR is on.
how: plugin-manager snapshots package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml before pnpm runs and restores them on failed install; removal proceeds bundle-from-profile, unload, pnpm remove, then runtime-resolution publication, stopping at the first failed step; Web approves the whole displayed group; replacing installed package versions needs a restart. Desktop runs a bundled pnpm via Electron Node. A proposed plugin-market index format would let third parties publish browsable indexes. The model-facing Creator tools (cordis_inspect_list, cordis_inspect_query) ship in the web-app agent preset named cordis (order 4, beside standard, minimal and ptc); the cordis host runner keeps process-local dynamic definitions in a node:vm realm for programmatic callers only, and no model tool creates them.
verevonRelevance: A transactional install/rollback flow with explicit failure table is the bar for any Verevon marketplace; remember DSH relies on npm, not signed manifests.
notes: Third-party plugins run with full Host authority and SAFETY.md says there is no audit.

name: Out-of-process control surfaces: stdio JSON-RPC SDK, Python SDK and automation-only ACP
what: Programs can drive a full runtime over newline-delimited JSON-RPC (TypeScript and Python clients) or the standard Agent Client Protocol, but the SDK wire has no prompt-cancel or session-close method.
how: SDK protocol: initialize, session/prompt, session/wait, working-directory get/set, shutdown; notifications session.event, session.status, subagent.started/finished; server never sends requests. Python SDK launches dsh --profile sdk with an explicit DSH_HOME (never ~/.dsh), returns RunResult from receipt to whole-agent idle. ACP supports create/resume, model and effort, MCP servers, prompts, cancel, semantic updates; no load/fork/terminals/elicitation. Verified in source: the SDK wire has six request methods (initialize, session/prompt, session/wait, session/working-directory get and set, shutdown) and four notifications; session.event carries the raw session-log event envelope for every session in the runtime. The Python client is synchronous and thread-based (a reader thread, per-request waiter queues, a 400-line stderr tail attached to transport errors), filters notifications to a session tree using subagent.started parent and child edges, requires an explicit DSH_HOME, and Session.run waits for the agent/inbox/spliced receipt of its own message id before collecting events until the whole agent reports idle. The bundled runtime ships as per-platform wheels (manylinux_2_28 x64 and arm64, macosx_14 arm64 and x64, win_amd64) built by a hatch hook that rejects mixed-platform payloads.
verevonRelevance: Shows the minimum viable embed API; Verevon's gateway should include cancel and close from day one and a run-interval result, which DSH callers must emulate.
notes: Both SDK projections must be updated with any loop or event change (AGENTS.md rule).

name: Compatibility bridges with other agent ecosystems
what: Existing Claude Code and Codex command hooks, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md files, SKILL.md skills and MCP servers work unchanged, and Claude Code mods can run as plugins through defineMod.
how: hooks-claude-code/hooks-codex bridges run command hooks (7 of 30 Claude Code events supported; PreToolUse deny/ask only, updatedInput not honored) through a shared hook-protocol; claude-code-mods implements the mods register(on, options) interface over harness services (AbovePrompt band only). Proposed notes cover Pi extensions and plugin compatibility levels.
verevonRelevance: Compatibility shims are a cheap adoption path: Verevon can accept Claude/Codex hook and skill formats to attract existing agent users while keeping policy in its own pipeline.
notes: All experimental and off by default.

name: System prompt assembly registry with ordered sections, scoped shadows and complete-prompt override
what: Prompt text comes from ordered sections contributed by owning plugins, with agent-scoped sections shadowing globals and an optional complete section replacing the whole prompt.
how: ctx.systemPrompt.section({name, order, text}) with centrally allocated first-party orders (identity -1000, persona 0, harness source 10000, Web surface 10100, persona suffix 10200); variables via {{name}} interpolation (unknown reference fails assembly); tool-schema providers return the visible set and pre-restriction universe for toolOrder; dynamic contexts become sourced user-role snapshots, not system text; refreshContext re-reads facts after pre-step. Verified in source: sections sort by numeric order then code-unit name (locale-independent, so the prompt is byte-identical on every machine), tools sort lexicographically unless a toolOrder with a reserved rest marker is configured (unknown names fail), a section may be marked complete to become the sole prompt (more than one fails assembly), and a separate CONTEXT_ORDERS table (working directory 100, sandbox 110, approval 115, delegation 120) orders the dynamic runtime-context snapshot.
verevonRelevance: Separating stable sections from dynamic context snapshots is the prerequisite for cache-stable prompts; Model Plane agent definitions could expose ordered prompt sections owned by plugins.
notes: No end-user prompt-editing API; deployment config/composition only.

name: Experimental packages ship off and are isolated from the default product
what: Capabilities under evaluation (browser use, computer use, agent teams, auto review, voice input, worktrees, terminals) are published but switched off unless a bundle or row enables them, and a gate keeps them out of default compositions.
how: packages/experimental/README.md defines status independent of publication; verify-default-product-isolation rejects experimental imports in default installs except bundles named in OPTIONAL_BUNDLES; official on-demand bundles (voice input, cot translation, session titles) appear in the Web Plugins page; plugin records for experimental packages are namespaced plugin:<owner>/<record> and ignorable.
verevonRelevance: A formal 'experimental, off by default, enforced by a gate' lane is a good release discipline for Verevon agent features such as computer use.

name: Pre-tool input rewrite is a documented unsolved design
what: Hooks cannot rewrite a pending tool call's arguments because the assistant message, audit event and UI all read the original arguments before execution.
how: Proposed note: a rewrite must be a pre-identity consistency transaction that changes assistant history, the tool/call audit record (with original retained) and presentation atomically, which needs the decision to move before the log commit. Until then pre-execute, Claude/Codex bridges and mods log and skip updatedInput.
verevonRelevance: Verevon policy engines that redact or normalise tool arguments (for example PII scrubbing) need this solved up front: decide before logging, or log both original and effective arguments.
notes: Proposed, not implemented.

name: Per-call file-effect sandbox policy with reported enforcement level
what: Every confined command runs under read-only or workspace-write policy resolved per call, and each result states whether enforcement was full or partial and whether a denial or runner failure occurred; unavailable confinement fails closed.
how: ctx.sandbox wraps argv in a same-world runner chosen by dsh-sandbox-local (bwrap or Landlock on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS, restricted-token ACL on Windows); SandboxEnforcement is full|partial; SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE instead of running unconfined; danger-full-access bypasses the seam. sandbox-policy resolves explicit approved mode, then the last sandbox/mode log event, then deployment default; session cwd is the immutable workspace root. After a denial the model may request one strictly wider mode for human approval. Verified in source: PLATFORM_CHAINS is bwrap then Landlock on Linux (arbitrated by a one-time functional probe that applies the real read-only profile and runs true), Seatbelt on macOS and the ACL runner on Windows as sole candidates without a probe; STATIC_ENFORCEMENT claims full for bwrap and Seatbelt and partial for windows-acl; a configured runnerCommand asserts full enforcement and must supply failure signatures; ConfinedArgv returns the backend's denialSignatures and exit-gated runnerFailureRules so a runner that failed before the command is never read as a denial.
verevonRelevance: Per-run enforcement reporting (full vs partial) is the right audit field for Model Plane sandboxes; do not claim isolation the backend cannot prove.
notes: Policy vocabulary is file effects only: no network, syscall, process or credential restrictions. Denial detection is a stderr dialect, so a matching app error can be misread as a denial.

name: Static Landlock launcher and POSIX flock addon (about 460 lines of C)
what: Linux confinement is a tiny static musl executable that sets no_new_privs, installs a Landlock allow-list on itself and execs the command; session locking uses a Node-API flock binding. Consumers never compile native code.
how: landlock-run --ro/--rw/-- argv with exit code 125 reserved for launcher failure and probe output 'fully enforced' or 'partially enforced (older ABI)'; ruleset inherited across execve up to ABI 5; platform packages (linux-x64/arm64 glibc+musl, darwin-x64/arm64) carry prebuilds, no Windows prebuild; the C test oracle checks flock semantics independently.
verevonRelevance: A launcher this small is trivially re-implementable in Rust (landlock crate) inside Model Plane sandboxes; keep the documented exit-code and probe contract so classification bugs like postmortem 0004 cannot recur.
notes: Postmortem 0004: the partial-enforcement notice shared a prefix with fatal failures and mislabeled ordinary non-zero exits as SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE.

name: Windows write-restricted token plus capability-SID ACL sandbox
what: On Windows, child processes run with a restricted Low-integrity token whose write access is granted only to the workspace and a private temp directory; the backend reports partial enforcement because reads and some ACL edge cases stay open.
how: AclSandbox builds a token with DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE|LUA_TOKEN|WRITE_RESTRICTED via CreateRestrictedToken, a per-workspace write SID and deny of the ambient parent ACE; spawn through CreateProcessAsUserW; TMP/TEMP rewritten to a private dir; grants materialise eagerly across the tree (tens of seconds on large workspaces); hard links alias objects; AppContainer-package-SID ACLs block reads; PowerShell starts ConstrainedLanguage under read-only. Bundled diagnosis skill repairs descriptors with an escalated call.
verevonRelevance: Rare, documented Windows write-confinement approach; relevant only if Verevon ever runs agent code on Windows hosts. Linux microVM/container sandboxes remain the cloud answer.
notes: Reads and network are unconfined on Windows; piped stdio capture is impossible for confined grandchildren (EPERM).

name: OS-owned managed process ranges (systemd scopes, Job Objects, fallback)
what: Killing a command kills every descendant: Linux commands run inside transient systemd user scopes, Windows ones inside Job Objects, and other hosts fall back to weaker process-group or scan-based ownership with a warning.
how: subprocess-local selects native ownership when systemd-run --expand-environment=no and a user manager exist (probes cached), Windows runner assigns the suspended target to a Job before it executes, terminals get the same range; teardown is kill then await done; terminate()/waitForExit() act on the whole range. Spawned commands receive a scrubbed environment (drops *KEY*/*PASSWORD*/*SECRET*/*TOKEN* by name heuristic). Completed output spill files persist until external cleanup.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane sandboxes (containers/microVMs) own process trees by construction; the rule to copy is 'dispose awaits quiescence and listeners close before kill'.
notes: macOS has no persistent owner and uses PGID fallback; a SIGKILL'd harness orphans LSP servers.

name: Execution-world principle: fs + subprocess define the world, PTY and LSP are portable consumers
what: Pointing the filesystem and subprocess providers at a remote sandbox moves Bash, persistent terminals and language servers with them, with no provider forks.
how: ctx.fs owns canonical process path, file URI and containment; ctx.subprocess owns executable lookup, spawn and spawnTerminal with a handle whose terminate() reaches quiescence for its whole range; dsh-terminal-bash and dsh-lsp-stdio use only those seams. The host keeps Cordis objects, loop, session log, model transport, authority and skills; a remote provider owns files and processes only. No workspace synchronisation is implied.
verevonRelevance: This is the cleanest statement of the Model Plane/Quarry boundary: reasoning stays in the plane, an execution world (fs+process+sandbox) is swappable and carries all tool consumers.
notes: Remote workspace UI paths still assume host filesystem access (ssh README).

name: POSIX SSH execution helper with verified artifacts and no remote Node
what: A host can run commands, terminals, file operations and a PTC worker on a remote POSIX machine through one installed helper over an OpenSSH alias, without installing Node or npm packages there.
how: dsh-ssh verifies installed artifact digests before readiness; paired fs-ssh, subprocess-ssh (fd 7 control channel, independent stdout/stderr channels) and sandbox-ssh apply the remote machine's own sandbox backend; ssh-helper-runtime ships a relocatable single-executable archive (pkg --sea, per-target handshake probe and digest manifest) built by scripts/build-exe-for-ssh-helper.ts; helper cleans leases when the connection closes. Windows endpoints, provisioning and reconnect are not provided. Transport details (versioned RPC, reserved management budgets, TLS-PSK streams, client lease) are recorded separately in the SSH helper transport record.
verevonRelevance: Pattern for Verevon remote sandboxes: a small signed helper with digest-verified install and lease cleanup, speaking a multiplexed channel to the plane.
notes: No reconnect or replay; connection loss leaves remote termination unconfirmed.

name: Read-before-edit with version tokens and guarded atomic writes
what: File edits require a prior read of that file in the session and are rejected if the file changed since; creation is protected against concurrent creation.
how: fs-observation-policy listens to fs/write-intent and fs/edit-intent and fs/observed events; fs-local version tokens combine device, inode, size and nanosecond mtime/ctime; writes publish atomically (staging directory, rename; createIfAbsent uses hard-link publication) and preserve permissions; mutation lock is in-process only; observed state is not persisted across resume.
verevonRelevance: Lost-update protection for agent edits is a must for Verevon workspace documents; use content-version tokens from the Data Plane instead of inode metadata.
notes: Direct ctx.fs reads emit no fs/observed; authorisation is version freshness, not view completeness.

name: Two-layer write confinement: policy fence in the fs backend plus OS sandbox
what: File tools are checked against the session sandbox mode by a trusted-code fence, while shell commands are confined by the kernel; the fence is documented as not a kernel boundary.
how: dsh-fs-sandbox rejects every mutation in read-only and permits only the workspace and platform temp roots in workspace-write; writable roots are shared with the Seatbelt profile to prevent drift; residual resolve-to-syscall TOCTOU is narrowed by in-place re-canonicalisation but not eliminated.
verevonRelevance: Same layering Verevon will need: in-process path policy for fast feedback and a kernel/VM boundary for guarantees.

name: Persistent shell and terminal tools with tiered readiness detection
what: An opt-in persistent bash/pwsh keeps cwd, env, functions and background jobs across calls using a PTY; readiness is detected by prompt marker, silence and, where provable, an exact stdin-wait signal.
how: tool-bash-persistent/tool-pwsh-persistent on ctx.terminals + dsh-terminal-bash (headless xterm for control-sequence replies, line-oriented bounded scrollback); an interactive foreground child returns early with partial output only on Linux where the subprocess provider proves the stdin wait; exit, timeout or cancel resets the shell. Terminals are owner-scoped, process-local and die with the host; six terminal_* tools exist as an experimental bundle. Default bash/pwsh stay fresh non-login shells with no rc files. Verified in source: a send settles through three tiers. (1) stdin_read when the controlled prompt marker and its printable tail ('dsh> ') were seen, output has been idle for the poll interval and the foreground process group equals the recorded shell group; (2) stdin_read from an exact probe after exactProbeAfterMs when the subprocess provider proves the foreground group is waiting on input; (3) inferred_idle after idleSilenceMs plus a handoff grace (and a prompt-tail grace while the tail is still pending), so a child that inherits PROMPT_COMMAND cannot suppress readiness until the absolute timeout. Output is parsed through a headless xterm and retained in a bounded line buffer.
verevonRelevance: Persistent PTY tools are a UX gain but a reliability tax; keep the fresh-shell default and make persistence an explicit, owner-scoped preset choice as DSH does.
notes: PowerShell echo and PSReadLine quirks leak into partial output on Windows.

name: Browser-use and computer-use as exclusive provider seams over MCP or native drivers
what: One browser provider (Playwright MCP, Chrome DevTools MCP, Stagehand) and one computer-use provider (Cua Driver MCP or native) can be enabled per deployment; each contributes its own tools while the seam owns lifecycle and session isolation.
how: ctx.browserUse / ctx.computerUse reject a second provider by name; browser-use-runtime reuses a browser across a session's turns, closes it on session disposal, serialises operations per session, discovers MCP tools before the first request and offers attachment mode reserving one external browser; screenshots reach models through durable attachments; the shared desktop is not reserved per session.
verevonRelevance: Confirms the Verevon rule (Model proposes, Quarry executes): DSH has no policy layer between model and browser beyond approvals, and no per-domain grant model.
notes: All experimental; abort cannot undo delivered browser/desktop input.

name: Safe git worktree creation for the same session (experimental)
what: A session can continue in an isolated checkout created from a local commit on a new branch, with the existing sandbox governing writes.
how: ctx.worktrees / create_worktree uses Git 2.45+ with --no-lazy-fetch, skips configured filters to avoid executing repository programs or implicit downloads, leaves LFS pointers/encrypted blobs as stored, does not init submodules or copy uncommitted files, and retains branch and files when leaving; subprocess and filesystem must share an execution world.
verevonRelevance: Worktree-per-task isolation is a safe parallelism primitive for Verevon code tasks; copy the 'no filters, no lazy fetch' hardening.

name: Bundled primary runtime (Python, Node, pnpm, Office libraries) installed offline on first use
what: Desktop and the Python wheels carry or download a self-contained Python/Node/pnpm payload and Office libraries, and the load_workspace_dependencies tool returns absolute interpreter and library paths instead of the model probing the system.
