how: Desktop resources/runtime/primary-runtime is copied under $DSH_HOME/dsh-runtimes on first use (runtime.json records a digest of locked inputs; a changed payload replaces the directory after a complete staged copy); Python wheels download Office sidecars and the primary runtime explicitly with archive-hash verification and atomic publish; Office skills use python-docx/python-pptx/openpyxl plus a shared structural checker; LibreOffice Kit (independent npm package) renders and converts. SDK startup never downloads.
verevonRelevance: A locked, hash-verified runtime payload given to the sandbox avoids 'pip install in the sandbox' drift; Verevon sandboxes could preload a versioned data-science image the same way.
notes: Linux payloads require glibc; Windows payloads must be executable in place.

name: Per-turn workspace change cards from git temp-index snapshots plus whole-file copies
what: Each top-level turn gets a list of changed files with line counts and turn-start versus turn-end comparisons, even for files git does not cover.
how: workspace-changes snapshots the working tree at turn start and end through git and diffs them (two git features can still write into the repository git directory: core.splitIndex shared indexes and git-lfs objects); every file a file tool edits is copied whole before its first edit; non-git directories list only file-tool edits. Summaries live only as long as the Host process and the session. Comparison serves complete text including ignored files and paths outside the workspace.
verevonRelevance: Review-by-diff without a full checkpoint system; Verevon file/workspace artifacts could snapshot per run in the Data Plane instead (and add restore, which DSH lacks).
notes: Observation only: no restore or rewind of file edits.

name: Bundled ripgrep glob and grep with sampled over-cap results and spill recovery
what: glob and grep run on a bundled ripgrep without host installation, return workdir-relative bounded pages with truncated flags, include ignored files, and can sample an over-cap glob across top-level directories.
how: tool-fs-search uses @vscode/ripgrep (Python single-file runtimes ship a -rg sidecar); caps bound inline output; sampleOverCapGlobResults (false in base) balances by first path segment; an optional spill store keeps capped output recoverable; results report truncation so a capped result is never shown as complete.
verevonRelevance: Standard; the truncated flag discipline matters for Verevon search tools that feed models.
notes: No semantic/embedding index anywhere (scout negative).

name: Office authoring skills with structural checker and LibreOffice Kit sidecar
what: The agent loads Word, PowerPoint and Excel workflows that create or edit documents with bundled Python libraries, run a shared structural checker and optionally render pages, convert to PDF or recalculate workbooks through LibreOffice Kit.
how: skill-office registers office-docx/pptx/xlsx skills (assetRoot configurable); Python SDK exposes convert, recalculate and render_images without an agent; the checker validates DOCX/PPTX/XLSX only and does not judge pagination, fonts or chart appearance; Desktop registers the skills by default and Office-to-PDF conversion uses LibreOffice natively or a Node WASM engine with bounded queues.
verevonRelevance: A checked-skill approach to document generation (create, reopen, structurally verify, then deliver) is a template for Verevon docs/slides/sheets creation.
notes: No visual QA unless a render_document tool is composed.

name: Hardened anonymous web_fetch with destination pinning and sanitised markdown
what: Fetch accepts only public HTTP(S) destinations, resolves and validates every destination, pins the actual connection, strips active and hidden HTML, converts to markdown under a nesting guard and labels the body as untrusted.
how: web-fetch-http uses undici with DNS validation and pinned connections and the HTTP proxy policy; tool-web renders via turndown + GFM plugin in a real DOM with a 512-level nesting guard and a synchronous conversion cap; output is bounded as a whole with a truncation footer; web_fetch takes only url (no format or prompt mode) and does not request approval in shipped presets. Verified in source: URLs are capped at 2048 characters, http and https only, with embedded credentials rejected; a redirect that leaves the origin (scheme, host, port) is refused so each new origin needs a fresh tool call and public-address validation; non-2xx responses are results; only html and text-like content types are decoded, with the declared charset (an unknown charset fails loudly); the public-address check includes NAT64 prefix discovery so a translated IPv6 address cannot smuggle a private IPv4 destination, and the validated addresses are pinned into a per-request lookup; every result body is prefixed with the untrusted-content notice.
verevonRelevance: SSRF-safe fetching (resolve, validate, pin) is a requirement for Quarry-adjacent fetch tools; note that exfiltration to a public URL is not gated.
notes: Plain HTTP fetch with HTML-to-markdown conversion; pages needing JavaScript rendering would need the experimental browser tools (INF).

name: Cross-session references as immutable untrusted snapshots; content search is opt-in and off by default
what: A user can reference another session with @label; the service injects a bounded read-only snapshot flagged as untrusted background. Full-text session search exists but is off in shipped compositions.
how: session-reference ranks candidates by working-directory affinity, labels them from projections (never reads a log per keystroke), and prepares snapshots with a fixed warning forbidding following instructions inside them; session-query-sqlite (FTS5, unicode61) is mounted with path ':memory:' and openAt: never in base, so search fails with SESSION_QUERY_SEARCH_DISABLED; the experimental session-search bundle (five read-only tools) ships off. Resolves the scout's open item on tool-session-query shipped status.
verevonRelevance: Gives a safe cross-conversation context primitive (snapshot + untrusted warning); Hermes-style memory is still absent, so this is not a learning loop.
notes: SQLite DatabaseSync blocks the event loop during MATCH; no per-caller authorisation.

name: Default-on upload of the full session log to the official model API
what: Unless disabled in Settings, every official DeepSeek request carries an incremental dsh_session_log field with the canonical session events (messages, tool arguments and results, workspace paths, feedback) up to 8 MiB per request, plus the active plugin package inventory.
how: session-log-deepseek (enabled: true by default, mounted in base and sdk-minimal) contributes the field through ctx.deepseekLlmApiExtensions after the base body is serialised; acceptance after HTTP 2xx appends session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted so the cursor survives restart (at-least-once); a gateway selected by baseURL receives the same data; the Web switch persists enabled; OTel upload is independent. The 2026-09-14 decision note explicitly supersedes the earlier opt-in default. Contradicts the scout inventory, which called it opt-in.
verevonRelevance: Do not copy: Verevon's ZDR rule requires opt-in, tenant-controlled and auditable log export. It is, however, a concrete example of a vendor-trajectory channel that Verevon must forbid for third-party agent backends and gateways.
notes: Quality 3 because the mechanism is robust (watermark, bounded, at-least-once) but the default is privacy-hostile for any enterprise setting.

name: Telemetry channels: feedback-only session release, anonymous install id, explicit product events
what: Session logs reach the OTel collector only after explicit user feedback; product analytics are explicit-event only; one random per-home UUID correlates feedback, telemetry and provider requests.
how: session-telemetry-otel mode FEEDBACK_ONLY (default) releases the canonical prefix through the feedback event, batches within a 4 MB request limit, 1 s transport timeout, gzip, memory-only queue; DISABLED constructs no transport; DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED opts the process out; anonymous-user-id stored at $DSH_HOME/.anonymous-user-id; redaction waterfall owned by consumers; delivery best-effort with no durable outbox.
verevonRelevance: Consent-gated release of a log prefix tied to explicit feedback is a usable pattern for Verevon quality feedback, provided ZDR tenants are excluded by policy.
notes: Collector endpoint is hard-coded to a DeepSeek service unless DSH_TELEMETRY_OTLP_URL overrides it.

name: Credential store with environment-first precedence, write-only UI and reference-based config
what: API keys live in a private harness-home file or the environment, are referenced by name in configuration, and are never returned by the UI; sessions of the web host are authenticated with an HMAC secret kept in the same store.
how: credentials-local resolves launch environment, then $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml, then project .env, then harness-home .env; adapters resolve references per request; settings-controller returns redacted descriptors and accepts writes without returning values; the browser-session HMAC secret is a grant record client-connection/browser-session; deleting it and restarting revokes all cookies. Config headers can still carry plain-string credentials the redactor never sees.
verevonRelevance: Reference-not-value config is the baseline; Verevon should add KMS-backed storage and per-tenant scoping which this single-user file store lacks.
notes: File store is plain YAML under the home directory.

name: One-shot approvals that fail closed, plus an LLM auto-reviewer (experimental)
what: Sensitive calls request a one-shot human decision; missing, failing or rogue answerers resolve as unavailable and the action is refused; an experimental reviewer model can answer for the user.
how: ctx.approval resolves ask to allowed-once | rejected | cancelled | unavailable (closed vocabulary; non-vocabulary returns normalise to unavailable) and appends audit events for request and outcome; policy 'never' rejects every ask without prompting and tells the model (NEVER_SENTENCE) not to request sandbox escalation; no allow-always, no grant store, request carries no tool arguments, valid only inside an open turn. auto-review sends five-section context to the agent's own model, allows executing with full access, and asks the user on denial; outer run_code and direct Node effects are not reviewed.
verevonRelevance: A closed-vocabulary, fail-closed approval seam with audit events is a good template for Model Plane/Quarry escalations; add persistent grants with scopes and expiry, and pass arguments to answerers.
notes: Auto review can allow unsafe actions and costs extra tokens; it is off by default.

name: Browser trust fence plus launch-token cookie for the local web host
what: The GUI host rejects cross-site and DNS-rebinding requests with media-type and Host/Origin checks and then requires a signed browser session minted from a per-process launch token; wildcard binds are refused and static assets stay public.
how: client-connection enforces application/json on /api POST (415), accepts only loopback, bind-address or --trusted-host authorities, then authenticates every Remote call, channel and WebSocket stream; GET /?token=... exchanges the process token for an HMAC-signed HttpOnly SameSite=Strict host-only cookie (30 days, no logout), Secure under native TLS; /plugins bundles and other non-index assets are not authenticated (serveBundle has no check). Reachability is the bind address; fence is a confused-deputy defence, not identity.
verevonRelevance: Refines the prior Verevon note ('no TLS, no auth'): auth and native TLS now exist, but it is still single-operator and plugin bundles are served unauthenticated. Verevon's gateway needs per-user identity regardless.
notes: Prior-analysis claim that plugin chunks are served unauthorised is confirmed at route level; the index (boot graph) is authenticated.

name: Defensive-patterns rulebook distilled from shipped bugs
what: A short, enforced list of bug-class rules covers orthogonal outcomes, public-contract normalisation, async-state pitfalls, quiescent disposal, listener containment, scrubbed environments, private temp files and link-safe deletion.
how: docs/defensive-patterns.md is referenced from AGENTS.md before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess or teardown work; companion rules sit in docs/testing.md (real entry path, verify the world) and the dsh-error-handling skill (typed structured failures, an empty catch names the error).
verevonRelevance: A living, short rulebook of past bug classes is cheap to adopt in the Rust/Go codebase and doubles as reviewer checklist.

name: Explicit unaudited developer-preview posture and plugin trust gap
what: The project states it is not secure or production-ready, that sandboxes and approvals only reduce risk, and that third-party plugins and model-generated code can damage the host.
how: SAFETY.md; presets are not security sandboxes (YAML and plugins execute Host code); the workflow VM and runtime plugin vm realm are not security boundaries; web_fetch exfiltration to public URLs is ungated; SDK/MCP-managed spawns bypass ctx.subprocess; no tenant/role/SSO model exists (single operator).
verevonRelevance: Honest labelling is worth copying, but Verevon needs the multi-tenant controls (org ACLs, SSO, audit export, ZDR) that DSH explicitly lacks.
notes: Negative findings on tenancy come from keyword sweeps (scout Appendix D).

name: Model-visible implies logged: every request is a pure function of the session log
what: Anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from durable session events, so any request can be re-derived, audited or replayed.
how: Surface events (system/message, developer/message, user/message, assistant/message, tool/result) carry the model-visible content; request/header stores a full canonical snapshot of the non-history envelope (call config, adapter defaults, assembled tools) with reason initial/resume/change/series; request/context records route capability; plugins that change message content register pure message projections (@messageProjection) so detached readers rebuild the same history; new model-visible inputs require a new session event.
verevonRelevance: The strongest transparency and ZDR-audit property in the repo: for Verevon it means support/compliance can prove exactly what a model saw; Model Plane should log a request envelope snapshot per series even if payloads are later purged.
notes: Cost: header snapshots grow per message series; assistant stream frames are lost on hard crash before settlement.

name: Per-package 'Model Experience' contract: what the model sees, token effect, KV-cache effect
what: Every package README that touches model input must state what text/schemas the model receives, the token cost, and how the change affects provider prefix reuse, enforced by a CI gate.
how: scripts/verify-package-readme-model-experience.ts validates the three headings, generated-catalog links and final-section order, with an audited allowlist of model-agnostic packages; scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts requires a canonical Known Limitations and Deferred Work section; the packages README states both contracts; docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md owns the template.
verevonRelevance: Directly adoptable by Model Plane: add a 'prompt/cache impact' field to every plugin/tool/skill definition and gate it in CI; it turns cache regressions into review-time findings.
notes: Prior Verevon analyses did not capture this documentation standard or its gates.

name: Embedded timed assistant streams, retained failed attempts and whole-session statistics
what: Each assistant message embeds the exact compact timed stream (token boundaries and timestamps) that produced it, failed or cancelled attempts are kept as assistant/attempt, and session stats report LLM, tool, first-token and decode wall times from the full log.
how: AssistantStreamAccumulator records chunks compactly (about one tenth the size of an expanded stream); assistant/message embeds it, assistant/attempt retains failed/retried/cancelled streams without adding model history; session-stats folds step counts and wall times from the durable log so paging and compaction do not change them; a hard process loss before settlement leaves no durable stream.
verevonRelevance: Latency telemetry (time to first token, decode time) falls out of the log for free; Verevon cost/latency dashboards could be log projections rather than separate metrics.
notes: Cancelled steps are counted but untimed.

name: Generated and boot-verified documentation with 60+ gates
what: The tool catalog, config catalog (152 plugin sections), persistence catalog, CLI help, module graph and seam graph are generated from live code and CI-compared, alongside 63 verify-* scripts and 18 generators.
how: gen-tool-catalog boots each tool plugin against a real context and reads its live schema; verify gates cover documentation links, bilingual pairing, mermaid, type-equiv doc code blocks, export JSDoc, README summaries, dependency policy, default-product isolation and application entry points; doc-sync aggregates them.
verevonRelevance: A generated catalog is the cheapest guard against doc/code drift (the Verevon stale-doc register is evidence the need exists); Model Plane could generate its tool/agent catalog from the registry in CI.
notes: Heavy process: 195 root scripts and 1,987 spec files to maintain.

name: Event-sourced session with derived surface and logged replacement operations
what: Sessions are append-only typed event logs; the model-visible conversation is a derived ordered 'surface' that compaction, tool-result pruning, image offload and prompt consolidation change only by logged replacement events citing the shadowed range.
how: SessionEventMap with per-event surfaceOp (append or replace {startSeq,endSeq}); replacement validates complete shadowed-node coverage and sourceEventSeqs; empty system/developer nodes project to no message; deriveMessages() caches deep-frozen projections; payloads are lossless-JSON validated at append by a one-pass snapshot (no BigInt, cycles, -0, exotic prototypes); system prompt is surface node 0 (protected from compaction).
verevonRelevance: A log + derived surface (instead of mutating message arrays) gives replay, fork, audit and compaction safety in one mechanism; the right backbone for Model Plane sessions/runs.
notes: Deprecated synchronous event readers still used in places (policy note 2026-09-09).

name: Crash-safe JSONL session store with immutable generations, adjacent migrations and a cross-process write lease
what: Each session is one append-only file of checksummed Zstandard frames (or plain lines); writes fsync per batch, torn tails are recovered, committed generations are never rewritten, and a kernel lock excludes a second writer process.
how: Header-first lazy materialisation via no-overwrite publish (link() on POSIX, write-through rename on Windows); fsync before append resolves, rollback on failed write; torn final frame truncated and rewritten from decoded records; checksum failure in a complete frame is corruption; session.vN.jsonl[.zstd] generations with adjacent vN to vN+1 migration packages checked gap-free at init; flock(2) on session.lock via the native addon or a named kernel semaphore on Windows; read open never publishes a successor.
verevonRelevance: Persisted-event schema evolution with immutable generations and adjacent-step migrations is a model for Verevon's run/session storage, even if the medium (Postgres rows) differs.
notes: No deletion/retention API; list() is unpaginated; POSIX needs hard-link support and the native addon.

name: Session-format governance: finalization record, release record and persistence-change review gate
what: Which session format the checkout writes, which is finalized and which has shipped are three separately recorded facts, and any persisted-type change requires an acknowledged, reviewed record.
how: SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION in core session types is the only hand-maintained writer number; docs/session-format-status.md holds latestFinalizedVersion and latestReleasedVersion with an evidence tag, checked by a doc-standard test; persistence-changes gates (finalized/v4.json, historical-formats, reviewing-persistence-type-changes cookbook) require review of declared type changes; alpha/beta/rc releases already create released-data obligations; equal-version unknown events must carry ignorable:true.
verevonRelevance: Treat persisted run/event schemas as released data from the first preview; adopt the three-record scheme (writer, finalized, released) in Model Plane docs/CI.

name: Projection seam with persisted projection cache
what: Client-visible per-session state (todos, goals, stats, token usage, user questions, inbox, subagent catalog) is folded incrementally from committed events by registered projection units and checkpointed so lists and restarts avoid replaying logs.
how: ctx.sessionProjections units fold events synchronously and expose typed values via stateOf() and batched snapshot() with the last reflected event; dsh-session-projection-cache stores version-stamped per-session checkpoints in the session_projcache storage domain with throttled write-behind (every 200 events or 5 s); a stale checkpoint is never ahead of committed events; the unit table is process-wide so key presence is not a per-session capability signal.
verevonRelevance: Event-fold projections with checkpoints are the scalable way to serve Verevon chat lists and agent status without joining raw events; cross-plane DB rules favour this over shared tables.
notes: Eager drive touches every unit per event; no per-key opt-out.

name: Typert: decorator-declared Remote RPC with generated schemas and clients
what: Host services mark methods with @Remote; the build analyses TypeScript types and generates strict descriptors, Zod codecs and typed client methods, so the browser calls ctx.remote.<namespace>.<method> with validated arguments and results.
how: A compiler-independent type-graph model feeds emitters for Host reflection (typert.host.js), Host-for-Client contribution (typert.remote-client.js plus declaration merges and source maps); lookup providers map wire ids (agentId, sessionId) to live Host objects and RemoteScope maps identities to scoped contexts; unary calls use POST /api/<namespace>/<method>; streams multiplex over /api/remote.mux WebSocket with half-close, uplink and cancellation; a source-mode fallback is weaker and refused by the client.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Rust gateway + SolidJS client can get the same property with schema-first generation (OpenAPI/specta/ts-rs); the lookup-provider idea (wire id to server object in one chokepoint) is the tenancy seam the prior analysis flagged.
notes: Resolver automatically resumes cold sessions, so a read-shaped call can allocate an agent (prior claim confirmed by docs/api-gateway.md and file-reference/skills notes).

name: Baseline-then-increments streams with connection generations and strict readiness handshake
what: Every browser stream starts with a complete baseline and then increments; a connection generation becomes visible only after the Host attaches listeners and sends ready, and reconnects replace local state from a fresh baseline.
how: The internal $events logical stream is the generation source (ready frame carries Host home); handshake warns at 3 s and aborts at 15 s; retry uses 50-100% jitter with caps 500 ms to 10 s; session follow() first frame carries header, tail page, cursor and projection baseline, later live events append by sequence, page() serves older history and gap repair; workspace follow() replaces the whole projection on reconnect (no cursor); ordinary notifications are not replayed, pending scoped waterfalls are. Verified in source: emit frames are broadcast to every connected client generation; each scoped waterfall is offered to every client, the first 'result' wins and cancel frames retract the others, and a waterfall raised while no client is attached stays pending and is delivered to the next client that connects.
verevonRelevance: Adopt the rule that a generation exists only after incremental observation is attached; it removes the 'stale result lands on the wrong thread' race class the prior Verevon analysis recorded.
notes: workspace.follow() has no incremental catch-up; one tab's display memory is not shared. Security consequence for multi-user use: no event or pending request is addressed to a specific user or session owner.

name: Browser-side plugin graph with lazy module table and combo bundle URLs
what: The Web client is itself a Cordis application: the Host writes a boot graph to window.__DSH_BOOT__, a lazy CommonJS module table loads combo bundles on demand, and every UI feature is a plugin contributing typed slots and settings cards.
how: ClientModuleRegistry serves /plugins/<combo> with revisions derived from entry mtime/ctime/size (no byte hashing), splits combos before the map-form URL exceeds 3 KiB, marks bundle responses no-store in Desktop; ui-renderer hydrates boot DOM then renders the sole 'root' slot; dsh.client package fields declare client modules; ConversationNodeDefinition registry lets plugins add chat node types.
verevonRelevance: A plugin-composed frontend is powerful but heavy; Verevon's SolidJS shell could borrow slot-based extension points for plane-owned panels without the custom module loader.
notes: React 18 + zustand + lexical stack; boot is all-or-nothing per prior analysis (not re-verified).

name: Single launcher rule and shipped profiles
what: Every supported Node application starts through dsh --profile <name>; package bins, demos and public SDK argv escapes are forbidden and verified by a gate.
how: Profiles web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal, acp (plus desktop) compose dsh-base or a standalone bundle; verify-application-entrypoints classifies every bin, executable and root script and rejects paths that bypass dsh; the TypeScript SDK resolves the same-version dsh and selects sdk; the Python wheel packages the same CLI.
verevonRelevance: One launcher with composition profiles prevents the 'many binaries, many configs' drift; Model Plane service binaries could share one composition loader with profile names.

name: Electron desktop shell around the full web host with task-aware quit and update journal
what: Desktop is an Electron shell that boots the same Web application through a RunAsNode Host child, hides to tray on close, and asks the Host what a quit would interrupt before exiting.
how: dsh-app:// scheme loads packaged Web assets; Host answers a private IPC inspection (running agents including subagents and approval waits, queued messages, running or stopping jobs, armed reminders) within a 2 s deadline; mandatory-update policy with journal, backoff and jitter; Windows EV signing and PE audit before sealing runtime hashes; bundled pnpm for plugin operations; microphone access limited to the primary frame.
verevonRelevance: Not a Verevon surface (web-first), but the 'ask the host what would be interrupted' pattern applies to deployments and tenant migrations of long-running agents.

name: Single-file executables and per-platform Python wheels for distribution
what: The full CLI, including the Web frontend, ships as a Node SEA executable (pkg --sea) inside Python wheels for five platform tags and as an SSH helper archive, so no system Node is required.
how: build-exe-for-python-sdk stages a symlink-free closure manifest (dsh-python-runtime-closure), asset globs cover Cordis runtime imports pkg cannot see, resolution uses an in-memory generation instead of disk symlinks; wheels carry the executable, ripgrep sidecar and node-pty helper; version is stamped from the repository version at wheel build; optional Office/primary-runtime payloads are explicit downloads with hash verification.
verevonRelevance: Shows the cost of shipping a Node agent as an executable (assets globs, native sidecars, patched pkg); a Rust Model Plane binary avoids most of it, which is a point for the Rust rewrite.
notes: Resolves the scout's open item: Python manifests carry placeholder 0.0.0.dev0 and the wheel version comes from package.json at build.

name: Stable N-API native addon family with release matrix and packed-install rehearsal
what: The Landlock launcher and flock binding ship as prebuilt platform packages built on CI runners per OS/CPU/libc, packed and verified before publish, so installs never compile.
how: @deepseek-ai/node-addon-system entry package plus darwin-arm64/x64 and linux-arm64/x64 optional dependencies; stable Node-API removes the Node-major dimension (tested on Node 20, 22, 24, 26; Alpine for musl); platform prepack validates formats, architecture and exports; verify-packed-install installs local tarballs and exercises mechanisms; Windows uses koffi FFI with Job Objects and a named semaphore instead.
verevonRelevance: Confirms there is no Rust in the repo; the native footprint is small enough to rewrite in Rust inside the Model Plane sandbox crate.
notes: No Windows prebuild; koffi FFI carries the Windows binding table.

name: Vendored and rescoped framework with an exhaustive local-modification log and targeted dependency patches
what: The Cordis framework and foundation libraries are source-vendored under the vendor scope with 23 numbered local modifications, and seven pnpm patches fix third-party defects with documented reasons.
how: vendor/README.md logs each divergence (fiber lifecycle hardening, include patch-semantics export, volatile config, runtime-shape detection for Node loader internals, durable debounced writes, lazy config resolution); patches: pi-ai (stop O(n^2) re-parse of streamed tool-call arguments), node-pty (embedded helper path, ConPTY drain), pkg SEA (atomic addon extraction), exceljs (OOXML prefix tolerance), fortune-sheet (two), osx-sign; a rescope script maps names and a hygiene check asserts the post-state.
verevonRelevance: Own what you build on: Verevon should vendor or pin core agent dependencies and keep a divergence log; the pi-ai patch shows how a multi-megabyte tool-argument stream can stall every session in a single-process host.
notes: Single event-loop host: one O(n^2) parse stalls every session in the process.

name: Entire harness hosted in a browser Web Worker (experimental preview)
what: A packed virtual-filesystem image of the real build products runs the full plugin tree inside one dedicated Web Worker with a Node compatibility layer, an in-worker shell and an HTTP-over-postMessage tunnel, for serverless previews.
how: webworker-packer builds a three-layer image (roster, publish view, reachability sweep with lowering to a wrapper contract); webworker-runtime provides node:* shims over VFS, a child_process implementation that spawns shell Workers, readable-stream, AsyncLocalStorage snapshots; node:vm/net/dns/sqlite/worker_threads are loud stubs; JSONL logs stay plaintext (no zstd); PTC Node programs and package operations are unavailable; deployed via Cloudflare Pages preview workflow.
verevonRelevance: Not needed for cloud Verevon, but a client-side-only demo mode (no backend) is a conceivable sales/preview path; shows the cost of Node-compat layers that a Rust/WASM core avoids.
notes: Experimental; mismatch between worker and Node behaviour is managed by acceptance tests only.

name: Host-plane versus agent-plane ownership criterion after per-session presets
what: Services that rows outside a preset realm read, or that own process-wide projections (jobs registry, goals, token meter, subagent registry, skill registry), stay on the host; only per-agent contributions move behind presets.
how: Decision note 2026-08-10: moving the token meter into preset realms made the context meter depend on which presets happened to be mounted; an agent that joined no preset silently saw empty tools, system prompt and skill views (no error). Resolution: meter returns to host, entry points must join agents to a preset explicitly, projection key presence is not a capability signal.
verevonRelevance: A concrete lesson for Verevon per-agent capability scoping: process-wide registries and per-agent scopes must be separated explicitly, and a missing scope should fail loudly, not yield an empty tool list.

name: Single-process, single-host state model
what: Jobs, terminals, subagent activations and ownership graph, approvals, schedules delivery, goal continuation, projections and storage-domain change events are process-local; there is no multi-process coordination beyond the session write lease.
how: jobs contract is in-process; subagent Activation inbox and ownership graph do not coordinate two harness processes; terminals die with the host; storage-domain domain/changed is an in-process event and the JSON backend has no cross-process write lock; schedule delivery needs the Host running; agent-team broadcasts whole views to every browser.
verevonRelevance: The core architectural gap versus a multi-tenant cloud plane: Model Plane must keep run/job/approval state durable and lease-based, which DSH explicitly defers.
notes: Consistent with its local-first, single-operator design.

name: Rust-portable design patterns found in the harness
what: Several load-bearing patterns translate directly to Rust and Go: branded ids, merge-extensible typed event maps, append-only log plus derived projections, explicit resolve(request) to Spec steps, generation-based migrations, disposer-returning registrations.
how: AGENTS.md conventions: opaque ids branded (Branded<B>), switch on discriminants with assertNever, explicit resolve(request): Spec instead of hidden defaults in run(), registrations are effects with disposers, no hardcoded tunables (validated Config fields), misconfiguration fails loud at load, trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries but validate at parser/config/queue/model/durable/file/worker/process/wire boundaries. Additional portable patterns verified in pass 3: closed typed failure taxonomies returned as fields of a resolved result (PtcRunFailure, ToolExecutionResult), explicit per-call policy objects instead of ambient state, memoized reverse-order teardown, and boundary frames rebuilt field by field before use.
verevonRelevance: A ready-made convention list for the Rust Model Plane: newtype ids, enum-per-event with exhaustive match, spec-resolution step, explicit boundary validation.
notes: Basis: repo conventions read directly; the portability judgement is inference.

name: Decision-record, postmortem and limitation-first engineering culture
what: Design decisions (implemented, archived, proposed, rejected), four blameless postmortems and mandatory 'Known Limitations' sections make the project's trade-offs searchable and frozen once archived.
how: .agents/notes holds about 2,450 markdown notes (implemented 504, archived 1,849, proposed 82, rejected 16) with status classification gates; postmortems pair a root cause with a guardrail and a Landlock-style regression proof; archived notes are frozen and never edited; every package README ends with limitations; agent notes are written only for durable decision rationale.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already adopted a postmortem and rejected-design ledger (adoption plan 7.6); the extra idea is the machine-checked classification and the 'proposed' lane acting as roadmap.
notes: Note counts from directory counts (SRC).

name: Keyless recorded-session replay corpus across headless, SDK, ACP and Web
what: Recorded model transcripts replay through the real shipped profiles without an API key, and the resulting session logs, workspace trees and browser/ARIA output are compared to committed expectations.
how: llm-replay replays each parent and subagent session's script in first-call order from session JSONL fixtures, with a replay.override.json sidecar for pre-chunk failures, cancellation, hangs and injected retries; session-snapshot provides manifests, typed identity redaction, workspace comparison and adapters; 227 scenarios (136 session, 59 web, 26 sdk, 10 acp); record needs a key, refresh does not; any model- or human-visible change must update a scenario; loop/session/event changes must update both SDK projections.
verevonRelevance: The most reusable eval asset for Verevon: recorded transcripts replayed through the real agent stack give deterministic regression tests for Model Plane flows without model cost.
notes: Fixtures replay on macOS/Linux only (AGENTS.md); no agent-quality scoring.

name: Scriptable mock model server with fault injection and seeded stress mode
what: A Messages-compatible HTTP/SSE endpoint scripts resets, stalls, malformed chunks, rate limits, server errors, completions and tool calls so recovery paths are tested against the real adapter and loop.
how: llm-mock-server consumes the next scripted behaviour per /v1/messages request, exposes captured requests, runs with pnpm run mock:llm or startMockLlmServer, and supports seeded random mixed-failure runs; recovery tests separate pre/post-chunk failures and prove failed chunks derive no message or tool side effect.
verevonRelevance: A provider-fault simulator at the HTTP boundary is a good Model Plane gateway test fixture (retries, idle timeouts, partial streams).

name: Test discipline: per-file 100% coverage on src, real entry path, verify the world
what: CI gates 100% line coverage per source file, requires non-unit tests that boot shipped profiles through the real Loader and built artifacts, and forbids asserting an agent's own report instead of the filesystem or process state.
how: test:coverage per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src (uncovered lines are often dead code); test resolution is source-plane only, built artifacts only in explicit lib-mode smokes; e2e assertions re-run the command or re-read files and assert untouched files byte-identical; real-API tests self-skip without a key ('inference is cheap here'); every registry needs an HMR-safety test; about 1,987 spec and 295 e2e files exist.
verevonRelevance: 'Verify the world, not the self-report' and boot-the-real-composition tests are directly adoptable for Verevon agent QA; the per-file 100% gate is optional.
notes: Line coverage is acknowledged as necessary, not sufficient.

name: Performance budgets for user paths, run in fresh child processes
what: Repository-level benchmarks measure stream reconnect, agent continuation, conversation fold, long-session browser, session open and corpus listing against reviewed constants, with CPU time, peak RSS and an HTML report.
how: benchmarks/ organised by user path; timed code runs in built workers under plain Node (no TS loader) in fresh children with private temp roots; synthetic inputs only; recordTimings/recordPeakMemory with BenchmarkCase metadata; environment variables cannot override budgets; test:bench:memory reruns files inside a swapless cgroup capped at 4 or 8 GiB.
verevonRelevance: Budgeted user-path benchmarks (session open, long-session render, reconnect) are the right protection against the long-session scaling regressions Verevon chat will hit.
notes: No model-quality benchmark ships (see next record).

name: No agent-task quality benchmark ships; external benchmarking uses the Python SDK and a minimal preset
what: The repository measures performance and determinism but has no task-success scoring suite; BENCHMARK.md only tells external harnesses to run the minimal SDK variant with separate workspaces and session ids.
how: BENCHMARK.md points to the Python SDK and the jsonrpc-agent minimal variant (the sdk-minimal profile: platform shell, local execution, JSONL sessions only); the Web minimal preset is a persistent-shell-only agent with a complete custom persona and no runtime context, which keeps prompts comparable across harnesses.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should build its own eval harness (task suites + scoring) on top of replay; a minimal-profile baseline (shell only, no runtime context) is a useful control arm.
notes: Absence inferred from directory structure and doc review; not proven by a full-repo semantic search.

name: Proposed: recallable compaction (index stubs, state checkpoint, history_read)
what: A design note proposes making compaction reversible for the model: frozen chronological index stubs with code-composed pointers, a mutable state checkpoint and an in-session tool to read shadowed spans back from the log.
how: Index chunks are compacted by compactRegion into ~100-200 token stubs with keyword anchors and a footer citing shadowed seq range; the model never writes pointers; stubs are never rewritten, reducing prefix-cache misses from head rewrites; slices of recalled content are stubbed by code only; failed stub calls degrade to pointer stubs.
verevonRelevance: Aligns with Hermes-style recall and with Verevon's append-only data: shadowed history stays retrievable by sequence, which could back a 'search my earlier context' tool.
notes: Proposed only; not implemented.

name: Tool-call lifecycle in three stages (preparing, start, result) with a lazy partial-JSON reader
what: Tool rows appear as soon as the model names a tool and call id, show live fields (path, content length, description) while arguments stream, then upgrade to the full card at dispatch and result.
how: The client Tool conversation node groups events by callId; PartialArguments (util/values/partial-json.ts) retains argument fragments with a top-level key/value range index and answers only the questions a row asks, refreshing at animation-frame publication; block-end and tool/call reconcile fragments against authoritative text; history pages skip the preparing stage; no server events or format changes.
verevonRelevance: Immediate tool visibility removes the 'nothing happens for seconds' gap during long write calls; Verevon's agent page can derive the same states purely client-side from streamed deltas.
notes: A stream whose arguments precede the name is not scanned.

name: Proposed: declarative Task Surface and interactive side sessions with merge-back
what: Two proposals extend chat: a model-published declarative form (show_task_surface) whose submission becomes one user message, and a read-only advisor side session forked at the last completed turn that can merge one condensed note back.
how: Task Surface is a versioned declarative component model rendered by a normal Web plugin; a successful call ends the turn and the submission is one ordinary visible user message; side sessions reuse ctx.agents.create with the parent's balanced completed-turn prefix, keep the system prompt byte-identical to preserve cache, and merge back via a plugin-sourced context message.
verevonRelevance: Generative structured UI (without arbitrary code) and cache-preserving side chats are both attractive Verevon chat features; DSH shows a low-risk design for each.
notes: Both are proposed, not shipped.

name: Plugin-owned message projections and producer-owned message sources
what: Plugins can change how recorded events appear in model history (for example redact or reframe) through registered pure projections, and every injected message carries a typed source naming its producer.
how: Events marked @messageProjection require a registered definition before append or restore; Session caches immutable message updates; detached readers must supply the same definitions; MessageSourceMap is merge-extensible (user, model, runtime-context, tool-registry, ptc-mode, plugin sources); each additional message carries exactly one source.
verevonRelevance: Source-typed messages plus registered projections are how Verevon could apply tenant redaction or ZDR transforms to model-visible history while keeping stored history replayable.
notes: Missing definitions reject append and restore, so unloading a plugin blocks reads.

name: Volatile configuration references: live settings applied to the next operation without remounting
what: Fields declared live in a plugin's config schema change on the running instance (model route, reasoning effort, parallel tool cap, upload switch, image budgets) without disposing the plugin's services.
how: Schemastery .volatile() returns stable references to immutable snapshots; Loader diffs raw config by schema-declared volatile paths, re-parses and validates the candidate through the fiber's internal/config hook, commits references when ordinary effective values are unchanged, and emits loader/volatile-update; ordinary-field changes still remount. Operations capture values once, so in-flight calls keep the config they started with. Profile writes go through the Web config editor, which validates the complete candidate before touching disk.
verevonRelevance: Per-operation config capture plus a live/ordinary field split is a clean way to give Verevon tenants hot-applied settings (model route, budgets, feature switches) without restarting runs.
notes: Schemas reject independent volatile references inside dynamic containers.

name: Retained preset revisions: editing a preset never changes running agents
what: When a preset is edited, new sessions use the new composition while running agents and their children keep the exact revision (and tools) they started with until they dispose.
how: dsh-agent-preset-registry owns each revision's scope and Loader tree; agents link scopes to a revision, children inherit the parent's exact revision, updates retire the old revision, cold readers hold leases, and the final release disposes the retired tree; saves write the active profile patch with revision checks and profile locking and reject higher-priority overrides that would defeat the edit; session data records the preset identity only and restart resolves it against current config (a missing definition is rejected). The decision note mentions an agent_preset tool that was not found in the code or generated tool catalog (stale note, INF).
verevonRelevance: Immutable capability revisions per running agent are the right model for Verevon agent definitions: edits must not revoke tools mid-run; reference-counted retirement is the mechanism.
notes: Old executable revisions are process-local and lost on restart.

name: Content-addressed attachment store with per-route normalised image variants
what: Uploads are stored once by content, images are validated and normalised into cached per-route request versions, and other files are kept verbatim; session events carry only references, never paths, URLs or base64.
how: attachment-local stores objects under DSH_HOME with verified length/content on read, identical bytes deduplicated across display names, images normalised with Sharp (animated GIF keeps only the first frame, encoder version pins variants), request variants addressed by variantId so changing an encoder re-addresses future variants only; objects are never deleted automatically and are local to one machine; unsent composer drafts are not saved.
verevonRelevance: Content addressing plus per-route variants gives stable prefixes and cheap dedup; Verevon would back it with Data Plane object storage and a retention policy (DSH keeps everything forever).
notes: No garbage collection; local to one machine.

name: Outbound proxy policy from environment only; project .env cannot redirect traffic
what: All Node fetch traffic (model calls, search, page fetch, HTTP MCP) follows the standard proxy variables read once at launch, while a repository's own .env is refused as a source so a cloned project cannot reroute traffic.
how: dsh-util-http-proxy applies one policy to built-in fetch (loopback stays direct, unsupported proxy URLs are reported per scheme), NO_PROXY with host-plus-subdomain matching, credentials in the URL never printed back; diagnostics name the rejected variable only. Model-authored code (workflow workers, Node PTC processes) receives no proxy settings so it cannot read a proxy URL carrying a password; OTLP telemetry and literal private-address web_fetch stay direct.
verevonRelevance: Egress-control precedent: untrusted workspace files must not be able to change where model or fetch traffic goes; Verevon sandboxes need an enforced egress policy, which DSH's file-effect sandbox lacks.
notes: DSH does not read OS proxy settings; telemetry connects directly and fails where direct egress is blocked. llm-deepseek README still says raw fetch has no shared proxy configuration, which appears to predate this policy (INF).

name: Parent-owned subagent catalog with durable child descriptors
what: Local child sessions are listed under their parent by durable id and label, survive restart and can be messaged cold; children whose descriptors are unavailable remain visible as mode unknown without continuation rights.
how: The subagent service records task identity and terminal results in the parent log, stores a descriptor (provider, depth floor, options) per child, projects the catalog from session observations, and reads descendants sequentially (large cold trees accumulate storage latency); external one-shot children keep only parent-owned records; list_agents returns the complete stably ordered set with no pagination or deletion.
verevonRelevance: Durable parent-owned child catalogs are the basis for Verevon agent run trees and billing roll-ups; add pagination and deletion that DSH defers.

name: Runtime-context snapshots: changing facts appended as sourced messages only when they change
what: Facts that vary per session or step (sandbox mode and workspace, approval policy, delegation, time, working directory) reach the model as a runtime-context user message that is appended only when it differs from the last retained snapshot, never by editing the system prompt.
how: Context providers registered on ctx.systemPrompt render a snapshot string; RuntimeContextProjection compares it with the retained snapshot (tracked from session events and surface replacements) and creates a user/message with source {kind:'runtime-context', form:'snapshot', sections} when different; an empty rendering appends an explicit cleared marker so older snapshots no longer apply; refreshContext re-reads facts after pre-step and route preparation. Suppressible per scope except required contributions.
verevonRelevance: The cleanest way to carry per-run facts (tenant policy, ZDR state, permission mode, time) without touching the cached system prefix; Model Plane should emit them as delta snapshots in the message stream.
notes: Costs one retained message per change until compaction shadows it; suppression is all-or-nothing per scope.

name: Provider-neutral failure payload with stable codes, retry-after and request id
what: Every provider or transport failure becomes one serialisable LlmFailure so consumers route on code, never on message text, and retry policy is separate from classification.
how: LlmFailure {message, code, status?, providerRetryAfterMs?, requestId?, offloadImages?}; codes include NO_ADAPTER, MISSING_CREDENTIAL, INVALID_CREDENTIAL, AUTH, QUOTA, ACCOUNT_QUOTA, RATE_LIMIT, CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED, INVALID_REQUEST, SERVER, TRANSPORT, TIMEOUT, ABORTED, EMPTY_RESPONSE, STREAM_CLOSED, MALFORMED_RESPONSE, IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED, UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT, REQUEST_EXTENSION; every stream ends with exactly one terminal finish chunk (stop, tool-calls, max-tokens, aborted, error) and adapters may throw but the runtime normalises to a finish; usage precedes finish.
verevonRelevance: A closed code vocabulary with provider-neutral semantics (quota vs rate limit vs account quota) is what Verevon billing, retry and UI error states need from Model Plane.
notes: Provider HTTP status is unavailable through pi-ai error events.

name: Agent phase machine with wake latching across maintenance and aborted work
what: Input that arrives while an agent is cancelling, running setup or already aborted is never dropped and never joins the wrong turn: a waking message is latched and replayed once the agent is idle.
how: ReactLoopAgent holds one of three phases (idle, maintenance, running). send(message, target, wakeup) reclassifies a waking message sent into an aborted activity as next-turn, captured before the inbox splice so a reentrant cancel cannot change it; wakeDriver latches wakeRequested for maintenance or aborted drivers (never for disposal) and the driver's finally block replays it when the inbox still holds work; runMaintenance runs create/resume setup as an exclusive phase with its own AbortController; cancel clears the inbox unless keepInbox is set; followup, steer and inject are fixed presets of send.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane run controls (queue, steer, stop) need an explicit rule for input that arrives mid-cancel or mid-setup; a latch-and-replay phase machine avoids both dropped and duplicated turns.
notes: Record 002 covers the durable inbox; this is the lifecycle machine that consumes it. Disposal deliberately never latches so teardown cannot start a model turn.

name: Turn end vocabulary with sticky max-tokens and tool-concluded turns
what: Every turn closes with exactly one logged reason, and a successful tool can conclude the turn itself, so structured-output and plan-exit tools stop the loop without another model request.
how: step() returns completed, max-tokens or null (continue); turn() keeps max-tokens sticky so a later normal step cannot downgrade the outcome; a pre-step reject becomes blocked; abort copies only the typed cancel cause; other failures become a structured {message, code} or the LlmError failure. ToolRunContext.concludeTurn() marks a result concludesTurn, composites forward it from nested results, and executeToolCalls returns concluded so the step ends as completed. The serial agent/turn-stopping event runs before the loop breaks so plugins (goal driver, subagent runtime) can still append next-step input.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane run states should keep distinct end reasons and let a tool declare the run finished, which is how terminal structured-result tools end subagent runs on every provider.
notes: interrupted and forked endings come only from synthetic closers written by session repair (record 005).

name: Cold resume ordering: take write ownership, append crash closers, then publish
what: Resuming a persisted agent first excludes any second writer, repairs the interrupted tail of the log, and only then lets the agent appear in registries, so a crash mid-turn never leaves a half-open turn visible.
how: AgentLoop.resumeWith opens the persistence handle in write mode first (a live agent's handle holds the claim, so a concurrent resume of the same id fails), cold-reads the log, computes interruptedTurnClosers (missing tool errors, step/end, turn/end) and appends them through the same handle, seeds a Session with the persisted events plus closers, flushes the unstored suffix, runs the setup callback inside the maintenance phase, then publishes to the session and agent registries and awaits creation listeners; an abort at any await closes an abandoned handle. Fork seeds reuse the same closers with a 'forked' cause and different model-visible wording.
verevonRelevance: A resume path for Model Plane workers should acquire the run lease before reading state and repair the tail through the log, not in memory, so replays and audits see the same repair.
notes: Persistence supplies only a physically valid log; semantic repair is the agent layer's job (comment at index.ts:884).

name: Scoped agent lifecycle with memoized reverse teardown and rollback
what: Creating or resuming an agent builds a scope, driver, registry entries and a persistence handle that unwind in one memoized reverse order on dispose, setup failure, owner unload or factory shutdown, even when these race.
how: AgentLoop.prepare registers its teardown before any resource exists, over mutable slots, so an unload during construction finds a working disposer. The memoized teardown aborts the fused signal (caller, owner fiber, factory), waits for any in-progress publication, cancels with {kind:'disposed'} and awaits whenIdle, disposes the agent scope, closes the session write handle (draining routed events), leaves both registries, collects every failure and rejects once with an AggregateError. initializeAgent runs setup in the maintenance phase and rolls back with the setup error as the primary failure; FactoryOwnership tracks live agents and startup tasks and waits on them at plugin disposal.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane sandbox-backed runs need the same single-quiescence guarantee (cancel, drain, close store, deregister) regardless of which owner triggers teardown first.
notes: Relies on Cordis fibers and effects (vendored with local lifecycle hardening, record 105); a Rust port would express this with scoped guards or structured concurrency.

name: Mandatory canonical output contract: validated JSON value, pure render, replayable presentation
what: A tool cannot return free text. Its body returns a JSON value that the registry validates against a declared schema, freezes, and renders to model content through a pure function; the same value serves the model, UI cards and programmatic callers.
how: ToolDefinition.output is required: {schema, render(args, value), presentationMeta?}. createSuccessResult snapshots the value as lossless JSON, validates it (ToolOutputError, code INVALID_TOOL_OUTPUT), deep-freezes it, renders content blocks and optional presentation meta, each snapshot-validated. Optional projectContent runs before post-execute policies; finalizeContent is a last-mile transform invoked once for every outcome including pipeline failures; presentCall and presentResult are pure functions of args and result so a UI can rebuild cards from the log; timeoutMs and isConcurrencySafe are registry metadata that never reach the model.
verevonRelevance: One typed result value feeding the model text, the UI card and code-execution callers is a clean tool-result contract for Model Plane; it avoids parsing text results and keeps cards replayable.
notes: Complements 055 (definition DSL) and 056 (pipeline); the mandatory output schema is the part those records do not spell out.

name: Tool-returned follow-up context ordered after the tool result
what: A tool, or a composite such as run_code or workflow, can attach extra context messages that reach the model only after its own result and in call order, without breaking tool call and result pairing.
how: ToolRunContext.deferContext(UserMessage) collects per execution and surfaces as result.additionalContexts; a tools/post-execute decision may add more, and a block decision discards body-deferred context so only context the decision supplies survives. executeToolCalls hands each committed result's contexts to the loop, which splices them into the inbox next-step list; they enter the next request after every tool result of the step in model order.
verevonRelevance: Lets Model Plane tools return side-channel instructions or images without violating provider rules that every tool call needs an adjacent result.
notes: PTC mode uses it to carry image results as context (record 057).

name: PTC collapse: direct calls to non-transport tools are denied before the policy pipeline
what: In programmatic mode the only directly callable tool is run_code. A direct call to any other visible tool fails deterministically with a message telling the model to call it from inside a program.
how: ToolRuntime.collapses(name, scope, nested) is true when the call is not a nested sub-dispatch, the effective presentation mode for the scope is ptc, and the name is not run_code. createExecution then returns a final ToolNotFoundError result carrying a route hint before the pre-execute waterfall, approval ask and guards run, so no policy listener can observe or approve a call that can only fail. Nested sub-dispatches (parent token set) bypass the collapse and re-enter the full pipeline. The mode is resolved per agent scope so a ptc agent preset under a native deployment cannot bypass it.
verevonRelevance: Shows how to make a programmatic-tool mode safe: enforcement belongs in the registry, not in prompt text.
notes: Record 057 describes the mode; this is its enforcement predicate.

name: Mid-session model switch notice with per-step selection snapshot
what: Switching provider or model mid-conversation appends a durable notice telling the new model that earlier assistant turns came from another model; an effort-only change adds no notice.
how: installModelSelection wraps three Agent-scoped waterfalls: system-prompt/assemble snapshots the selected route and publishes provider and model variables; agent/request applies the snapshot to the call config and clears an inherited effort; agent/pre-step (prepended) appends a user-role message with source kind model-selection, text '[model changed: assistant turns above this point were generated by X; the session continues with Y]', when the snapshot differs from the last logged request header. A failure before the header persists repeats the notice on the next request, and a concurrent switch applies on a later step so prompt and route are never split.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's multi-model chat needs this notice plus a per-step snapshot to avoid mixed prompt and route requests; pair it with the replay-state stripping rule in record 040.
notes: The notice is a durable log message, so it appears in replays and forks rather than being a UI-only marker.

name: Closed role map with first-class developer and tool roles
what: Model-visible roles are a closed set (system, developer, user, assistant, tool) and each must have a persisted event type and adapter projection, so no unlogged extension role can reach a request.
how: Session format V4 stores a tool result as a role 'tool' message with toolCallId and source callId validated together; synthetic recovery results are built the same way. validateSessionEventData requires developer/message events and role developer to occur together, restricts tool-addition and tool-removal blocks to the developer role, and requires a headerSeq exactly when additions are present. The V3 to V4 migration lifts exactly one released tool-result wrapper and refuses nested wrappers before publication.
verevonRelevance: A closed, logged role vocabulary keeps replay, fork and provider adapters consistent; Model Plane message schemas should reject roles that have no durable event.
notes: Decision note rejected accepting both wrapper and native rows as dual representations.

name: Non-suppressible app attribution on every provider request
what: Every provider HTTP request carries a public User-Agent naming product, version and repository. Deployments can white-label it but cannot remove it.
how: AppIdentity {product, version read from package.json, url}; attributionHeaders(identity?) returns {user-agent: 'product/version (+url)'}; the LlmAdapter contract requires every adapter to merge it into each provider request and to prove it at the wire or in the library header hook. The identity carries no secrets, paths, session ids, prompt text or per-user values.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should tag outbound inference calls with a stable non-secret client identity for provider-side attribution and abuse handling, separate from per-purpose headers.
notes: Contrasts with the per-purpose x-deepseek-harness-* headers (record 044), which are identity-bearing.

name: Untrusted-content label on every fetched or searched web result
what: Every web_fetch and web_search result opens with a fixed notice that the text that follows is untrusted data, not instructions.
how: tool-web/trust.ts exports EXTERNAL_WEB_CONTENT_NOTICE. fetch.ts builds the header 'Fetched <url> (HTTP n)' followed by the notice before the converted body; search.ts places the notice first in its result parts, so provider-generated answers and snippets sit inside the labelled block.
verevonRelevance: A cheap baseline for any tool that returns external text; Model Plane should add structural separation and approval gating for actions taken after reading untrusted pages.
notes: Advisory text only. No taint tracking or egress gating was found in a keyword sweep of the repo (INF).

name: Subprocess seam: no implicit defaults, scrubbed environment, bounded collection with spill
what: Spawning a process requires the caller to state every stdio disposition, working directory, grace period and env entry. The child inherits a scrubbed environment, and collected output keeps a bounded tail plus an optional full spill file.
how: SubprocessSpawnSpec {argv, cwd, stdio{stdin, stdout, stderr, control?}, graceMs, signal, env}; env merges onto scrubbedParentEnv (credential-shaped and stale DSH_* names dropped; string values are explicit opt-ins; undefined is a tombstone). SubprocessCollect {maxBytes tail, spill.maxBytes}; collected.stdout.readFrom(byte) returns text, nextOffset, a lossy flag and the spill path, and whole-stream offsets let independent readers never consume each other's output. handle.terminate() and waitForExit() act on the same provider-managed range; the MCP stdio transport reuses scrubbedParentEnv so both share one scrub definition.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane executors should require explicit per-call output limits and env scrubbing and expose offset-based reads so UI tails and model reads cannot interfere.
notes: Name-based scrubbing is a heuristic (KEY, PASSWORD, SECRET, TOKEN); see record 069.

name: Dedicated control channel at fd 7 for host protocols that child output cannot forge
what: A spawned program can talk to the host over a separate byte channel, so its stdout and stderr, which may contain anything, can never impersonate protocol traffic.
how: stdio.control='pipe' yields handle.control, a raw Duplex. The child calls openInheritedControlChannel(), which consumes the DSH_SUBPROCESS_CONTROL marker and opens fd 7 (SUBPROCESS_CONTROL_FD). POSIX launchers preserve fd 7 across exec; Windows Job and restricted-token launchers place the pipe at CRT descriptor slot 7 with handle inheritance enabled only around process creation; the overlapped pipe lets the child speak first. The channel grants no capability: consumers own bounded framing, validation, backpressure and closure, and the provider closes open endpoints at disposal.
verevonRelevance: Quarry or Model Plane runners that execute generated code should use a dedicated control descriptor with host-side frame validation rather than parsing stdout.
notes: control.ts and types.ts are source-verified; the Windows launcher details (CRT slot 7, inheritance only around process creation, overlapped pipe) come from the decision note (DOC). The experimental Python PTC provider documents an fd-3 JSON-lines protocol instead (see the Python PTC record).

name: PTC runtime host-child protocol, resource ceilings and typed failure taxonomy
what: Model-written TypeScript runs in a fresh confined Node process that reaches host tools only through declared bindings, and every way a run can end maps to one of eight typed failures fed back to the model.
how: NodePtcRuntime.execute strips types by wrapping the program as an async function body, confines argv through ctx.sandbox unless mode is danger-full-access (recording enforcement and denial from the backend's denialSignatures), and spawns with stdin ignored plus a control pipe. The child resets process.env to a null-prototype dictionary. Host and child exchange length-framed JSON (ready, boot, log, call, reply, done); call ids must be strictly sequential, binding names must have been declared, arguments and results must be lossless JSON, pending calls are capped (128) and so are frame bytes (128 MiB), output (64 MiB), V8 old generation (512 MB) and wall time (120 s default, 600 s cap). Failures are exception, timeout, abort, worker-exit, invalid-output, output-limit, protocol and sandbox-unavailable; an error is a field on a resolved result, and the process range is terminated and drained before the result resolves.
verevonRelevance: A ready template for Model Plane code-execution tools: typed failure kinds, explicit ceilings, sequential-call-id validation and sandbox enforcement facts returned with every run.
notes: The deadline is wall-clock, not CPU; the child is treated as an untrusted peer even when it follows the control descriptor.

name: Experimental Python PTC provider: fd-3 JSON-lines with host-side frame rebuild
what: A private experimental provider runs model-written Python in a fresh CPython subprocess without file confinement, treating every frame the child sends as hostile.
how: Frames travel as JSON lines on the child's fd 3 (child to host: boot-ack, call, log, done; host to child: boot, run, reply). The host rebuilds each inbound frame field by field and drops anything that does not rebuild cleanly, so forged extra fields or a done frame carrying both value and error cannot mislead it; completions that are not lossless JSON or exceed the budget are rejected explicitly. Frames above a 64 MiB parse cap settle the run as worker-exit; resource ceilings include RLIMIT_AS; the sandbox runner is resolved before spawn.
verevonRelevance: Python is the likely language for data tasks in Verevon agents; the rebuild-every-frame rule and RLIMIT_AS budgeting transfer directly to a Rust sandbox host.
notes: README claims only; the provider source was not read. No file confinement, so it is not usable where file effects must be bounded.

name: Browser UI as a participant in the Host hook pipeline (forwarded emits and scoped waterfalls)
what: A fixed allowlist of Host events is forwarded to every connected browser; for waterfalls such as approval and user-question requests the UI is just another listener that answers or passes, so human-in-the-loop uses the same extension chain as plugins.
how: API_REMOTE_FORWARDED_EVENTS lists 27 events (25 emit, 2 waterfall: approval/request, user-questions/request). forwardWaterfall queues an agent-scoped invocation for the Gateway's internal $events stream; the Gateway offers it to every connected client generation and replays still-pending ones to a client that connects later. A client replies through the unary $events/result RPC bound to clientId and eventId with outcome next, result or rejected (strictly parsed); the first result wins and cancel frames retract the others, rejected cancels the Host waterfall with the error, and next from every client lets the Host chain continue. Emit frames are broadcast to all client queues; arguments must be lossless JSON; the browser registers with ctx.remote.$on('approval/request', (request, next) => ...).
verevonRelevance: Approvals and questions between Model Plane and the Frontend Plane can be modelled as awaited event waterfalls; Verevon must add per-user routing because DSH offers every event and every pending request to every connected client.
notes: Resolves two open items from the scout inventory: events are broadcast to every client (confirmed), and an approval raised with no browser attached stays pending and is replayed to the next client rather than failing closed. Single-operator design; no per-session or per-user addressing.

name: Architecture fitness gates implemented as syntax-aware (AST) repository checks
what: Rules that review prose misses are enforced by scripts that parse TypeScript, so renamed imports, shorthand properties and escaped identifiers cannot dodge them.
how: verify-no-bare-dispatcher forbids constructing an undici agent or passing a fetch dispatcher outside the proxy owner (the global dispatcher carries the user's proxy; an exemption needs a marker comment). verify-plugin-record-callers limits appendPluginRecord to experimental packages and requires production writes to name a record in PluginRecordMap. verify-no-unknown-casts rejects new 'as unknown' assertions and retires old ones through a SHA-256 baseline of syntax tokens. verify-default-product-isolation keeps experimental packages out of default installs, imports and compositions except named optional bundles. verify-runtime-closure checks the executable manifest supplies every plugin a shipped preset references. verify-product-use requires each maintained package to have effective product use or an explicit non-default role. verify-package-readme-limitations requires one canonical 'Known Limitations and Deferred Work' section per package.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's cross-plane invariants (no cross-plane DB access, ZDR propagation, Space ACLs never widening an owner ACL) are the kind of rules to encode as AST or dependency-graph gates instead of review notes.
notes: Complements 088 (defensive patterns) and 093 (generated docs). The baseline ratchet for unknown casts is a reusable technique for retiring tech debt without a flag day.

name: Typed binary results in Remote RPC as multipart attachments
what: Remote methods can return raw bytes (for example file previews) without base64: the generated codec detects byte buffers in result types and the response carries them as separate multipart parts.
how: Typert recursively recognises Uint8Array in unary result types (roots, optional fields, containers) and generates encode() and decode() codecs; the Gateway returns JSON-compatible metadata plus result-relative byte attachments, the Connection layer sends them as FormData parts while preserving the RPC envelope and correlation id, and Client declarations narrow each buffer to ArrayBuffer. workspaceFiles.readBytes takes one options object that independently selects a byte range and a base file for relative resolution.
verevonRelevance: A Rust gateway serving the SolidJS client can adopt the same split (JSON metadata plus binary parts) for document and image previews instead of base64 payloads.
notes: Decision text read; the generated codecs were not inspected.

name: Workspace file service: reads inherit backend authority, navigation stays workspace-scoped, no mutation, no agent activation
what: The browser can preview any file the session's filesystem backend may read, including paths outside the workspace, but directory listing and change feeds stay inside the workspace and the service has no write operation.
how: api/workspace-files exposes read, readBytes, stat, list and changes; read-type methods resolve relative paths from the workspace root but delegate authority to the Session filesystem backend (regular files only, symlinks refused, page and byte caps); list and changes reject or filter by workspace containment. The workspaceFileScope lookup resolves a live Session header or, for a cold one, SessionPersistence.stat, and never activates an Agent, reads the event body or falls back to a parent Session. HTML preview packages bounded static scripts and styles into an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe, an accepted trade-off because the browser keeps network access.
verevonRelevance: Shows the split Verevon needs for Space file previews: one authority decision at the backend, a narrower rule for navigation, and a read-only API surface.
notes: The sandboxed HTML preview deliberately leaves network access enabled for script-enabled documents.

name: Session working directory as logged state distinct from workspace origin and sandbox roots
what: The model or user can change a session's working directory; the change survives replay and resume and reaches the model as context, while existing shells and processes keep their own directories and the original project and permission roots stay fixed.
how: WorkingDirectoryService appends a 'working-directory/change' event {cwd} and folds a 'workingDirectory' projection; the immutable Session header retains the original project directory, and a missing directory is recovered to that origin when still available. A model-visible notice is produced from the transition (source kind 'working-directory'); the model tool is working_directory (read, or cd to an existing directory) and the SDK exposes get and set. Deployment defaultDirectory covers sessions with no recorded origin.
verevonRelevance: Separating mutable cwd from immutable workspace origin and sandbox root is the right model for Model Plane sessions that run in sandboxes mounted per Space.
notes: Experimental worktree tool uses the same change event after creating a branch checkout.

name: Read-only LSP navigation tool: opt-in, stateless and serialized per workspace
what: When a deployment configures language servers, the model gets one lsp tool for go-to-definition, find-references, go-to-implementation and hover, with bounded results grouped by file; it is not part of the shipped profiles.
how: dsh-lsp is the seam (provider chosen by file extension, normalized results, structured failures such as LSP_UNAVAILABLE); dsh-lsp-stdio maps extensions to language ids, starts one server per workspace on demand through the mounted filesystem and subprocess seams, reads each queried file afresh without retaining document state, and serializes queries per server and workspace; dsh-tool-lsp renders one-based UTF-16 positions. Generic JSON-RPC, rename, formatting, diagnostics and symbol lists are deliberately excluded. No shipped bundle or preset mounts these packages.
verevonRelevance: Verevon is not an IDE, but a navigation-only LSP tool is a precise way for coding agents to resolve symbols without full indexing; it pairs with sandboxed workspaces.
notes: Absence from shipped bundles checked by grep of packages/bundle (INF). A SIGKILL'd harness can orphan language servers (record 069).

name: Ownership-weighted pull-request approval computed from git blame
what: A PR is mergeable only when approval points reach two, where a one-point reviewer counts more when they own more of the old production lines the change touches; reviewers can delegate points.
how: The weighted-approval workflow publishes a commit status from reviews, permission and git blame: write-capable reviewers give one point (two for listed maintainers), a one-point approval is weighted min(2, 1 + 4 x ownedLines/totalLines) over modified or deleted old production lines classified by a Pygments-based script, author credit is min(100, mergedPRs) x 11/1000, a write-capable CHANGES_REQUESTED blocks, and /delegate @user transfers points until the delegator reviews again. The status job marks the head pending before setup so a stale success cannot persist.
verevonRelevance: Process lesson only: encode review authority in code with blame-based weighting for a multi-owner monorepo like CoresSystem; no product feature.
notes: Policy lists named maintainer accounts; CODEOWNERS-style alternatives were not compared.

name: Fail-loud process policy: uncaught errors are fatal and never resumed, with a bounded terminal release and crash reports
what: Any uncaught exception or unhandled rejection prints one labelled diagnostic and exits 1; the failed operation is never resumed, a terminal-owning surface gets a bounded chance to restore the terminal first, and the Desktop shell writes a crash report before showing its dialog.
how: installFailLoud registers the same handler on unhandledRejection and uncaughtException: it writes util.inspect(err) (not err.stack, which omits fs error code, syscall, path and cause chains) before awaiting an optional release hook for at most 2 s (FAIL_LOUD_RELEASE_TIMEOUT_MS, a referenced timer so a never-settling disposer cannot let the loop drain and exit 0), keeps the handler installed during release so a second failure cannot kill teardown, then exits 1. Rejections already handled by the startup audit are ignored.
