Desktop reportFatal awaits writeCrashReport for at most one second: source, backend-ready flag, versions, the complete inspected error and a 64 KiB tail of renderer console errors, owner-only under the logs directory with the ten newest kept. Spill files and failed client batch scripts degrade per item instead of failing the whole feature.
verevonRelevance: Rust services should treat unexpected panics the same way (diagnostic with full cause chain, bounded cleanup, abort) and keep best-effort paths such as spill from taking down a run.
notes: Born from two field failures diagnosed from screenshots; the note explains why resuming after a throw is rejected (half-applied state).

name: Web listener exposure rules: concrete bind address only, own-IP Host trust and native TLS with scheme-bound cookies
what: The Web host binds exactly one named address (loopback by default), refuses wildcard binds, trusts its own bind IP as a Host without inferring LAN interfaces, and can serve native TLS where cookies are bound to the HTTPS scheme.
how: webserver config host accepts one IPv4 or IPv6 literal; isWildcardHost rejects every spelling of the unspecified address (0.0.0.0, ::, mapped and expanded forms) at config load and in dsh web. The Host/Origin fence accepts the listener's own bind IP literal as Host on any port independent of trustedHosts; DNS names and proxies still need --trusted-host. Optional tls {certFile, keyFile} (paired --tls-cert and --tls-key) loads PEM files before binding and fails activation instead of falling back to HTTP; webServer.protocol alone drives the advertised URL, the non-loopback plain-HTTP warning and the Secure cookie attribute, and HTTPS cookie names and signed audiences include the https: scheme so an HTTP credential cannot replay on HTTPS. Desktop pins --host 127.0.0.1.
verevonRelevance: Local or self-hosted Verevon components (Model Plane workers, gateways) should refuse wildcard binds and bind trust to explicit addresses; certificate issuance stays with the operator.
notes: Complements the launch-token and cookie fence in 087. Certificates are read once per activation; rotation needs a reload or restart.

name: Runtime plugin-package resolution table swapped as immutable generations (no symlinks)
what: Plugin packages outside the profile's own dependency tree are found through an in-process resolver table with a fixed precedence, so package selections never persist as symlinks or generated proxy manifests and a change publishes atomically.
how: Profile startup computes one immutable RuntimeResolution and installs it into Node's ESM and CommonJS resolvers (installRuntimeInterception) and registers it for Harness-owned Workers; PluginPackages.replace publishes a complete successor with one reference swap. Precedence: installation manifest graph first (dependencies then peerDependencies breadth-first, first package under a name owns it), then selected bundle roots in profile order with names from the installation reserved, with profile-local and plugin-private node_modules still taking precedence. Lookup anchors use each package's real directory so ancestor searches follow where Node would execute it; the same table serves source launches, packaged executables and the Electron host.
verevonRelevance: Relevant only if Verevon ships user-installable plugin bundles into a Node or Deno host; the lesson is to resolve extensions through an immutable in-memory generation rather than filesystem links.
notes: Existence of the interception and worker registration was confirmed in source; the precedence algorithm is read from the decision note.

name: Blank-session reuse arbitrated by the writer lock
what: Opening a workspace reuses an existing empty session instead of piling up blanks, and two hosts sharing storage cannot both claim the same blank because ownership is decided by acquiring the session's writer lock.
how: The session catalog includes persisted blanks; startup restoration selects the saved blank and ordinary navigation selects the first eligible unarchived member. An explicit-id session.create resumes that session and acquires its writer before opening history; only a 'session/writer-held' error triggers creation of a new session, every other error propagates, and concurrent connects in one client share the acquisition and fallback. The agent keeps the acquired handle for its lifetime because probing ownership and releasing would leave a race; no PID or process identity enters persisted data or the Remote schema.
verevonRelevance: Using lock acquisition as the single arbiter (not check-then-acquire) is the right pattern for Model Plane session and run claims across multiple workers.
notes: Builds on the cross-process write lease in record 095.

name: Migration-aware reads: fork and projection reads refuse to trigger session-format migration
what: Expanding a subagent catalog or forking from the sidebar never silently migrates an old session; the host checks the stored format first and the client shows 'Migration required' with an action to open the original.
how: The fork request carries allowMigration: false; the controller checks stat.formatStatus before the original fork flow and throws session/migration-required only when the source needs migration and is not live (other callers allow automatic migration). session.projections also checks stored format first: current-format cold history is read as usual and returns kind 'sequenced' with the real asOfSeq, required migration returns 'migration-required' hints; Web marks the row without descendant expansion and keeps its history-opening actions; cached values cannot replace sequenced ones.
verevonRelevance: When Model Plane run schemas evolve, read paths should distinguish 'needs migration' from 'unreadable' instead of migrating as a side effect of browsing.
notes: The note also confirms the resolver can activate cold sessions for some reads; the workspace-file scope lookup deliberately does not.

name: Host-state storage hub: schema-validated key-value domains over swappable JSON or SQLite backends
what: Application state that is not session history (schedules, workspaces, projection checkpoints) lives in typed domains where reads are synchronous from validated memory and each write is durable before it resolves, with the backend selectable per deployment.
how: ctx.storageDomain opens domains over the storage hub; writes become durable then emit ordered 'domain/changed' events; backend json keeps one file per unit ('single' layout) or one version-stamped document per record ('per-record'), published atomically, while sqlite stores one JSON document per row so a single record update touches one row; the base bundle mounts storage-json under DSH_HOME/storages with the projection cache using per-record layout. This state adds no tools, prompts or session events and is invisible to the model.
verevonRelevance: A small typed domain layer with an explicit choice between inspectable files and one queryable database mirrors Verevon's need to keep plane-local state out of the event log.
notes: Used by schedule, workspace and projection cache; no multi-writer or multi-host semantics.

name: On-demand reasoning translation with durable session-bound records and a cost-isolated paid path
what: Users can read a model's expanded reasoning in their language; translations are saved with the session, reused after restart, never replace the original or enter model input, and the paid route is isolated from the conversation's identity and history.
how: The experimental translator writes plugin:translator/request (provider, exact source text, source and target language, recipe identity, optional model request) before dispatch and plugin:translator/result (requestSeq, text) before returning, through appendPluginRecord on the live session writer; identity includes provider and recipe so settings changes cannot substitute another result; identical concurrent requests share one result and read-only cache lookup precedes provider work. Default Bing or Google routing needs no key; the paid route qualifies only built-in deepseek-account or deepseek-official owners with the exact deepseek-flash id, sends each fragment as a fresh text-only query with thinking disabled and no history, and withholds the main session identity so a fragment cannot authorize uploading the conversation log. Only expanded bodies start translation and collapse aborts it.
verevonRelevance: For Norwegian and multilingual Verevon users, translating visible reasoning on demand with durable, tenant-scoped, ZDR-aware records is a concrete transparency feature; the disclosure that text leaves to an external service must be explicit.
notes: Experimental and off by default; the Host does not verify that supplied text belongs to the named session (decision note). Complements the privacy disclosure noted in the sibling transparency facet.

name: Workspace registry: project directories with grouped sessions and an archive admission handshake
what: Projects are an ordered persistent list of directories with their sessions, invisible to the model; archiving a session asks each owner what still runs and cancels the live turn without leaving queued input to wake it later.
how: packages/workspace stores the ordered list; removing a project never deletes folders, files or session histories, and re-adding a directory creates a fresh project; sessions whose directories cannot be validated stay ungrouped. Archive admission is a waterfall: each owner answers workspace/session-activity with its own activity family - the agent (a running turn, including one waiting for approval or an answer), the job registry (running or stopping jobs), the subagent service (running descendants) and the schedule service (armed reminders, so an idle session with pending reminders refuses the archive) - and workspace/session-stop cancels each: the turn like the user's stop but without keepInbox so queued input is discarded with a logged splice, descendants as their parent would, and reminder rows are deleted instead of delivering into a closed session. api/workspace-controller exposes create, rename, remove, reorder, archive, unarchive and a followable complete projection.
verevonRelevance: The 'ask every owner what is still running, then stop without waking later' handshake is a clean pattern for archiving or deleting Verevon chats that own agent runs and background jobs.
notes: Directory-centric, not topic-centric; UI side is covered in the sibling transparency facet. Each owner contributes a typed activity family, so new background-work owners join the handshake without changing the registry.

name: Request-extension registry: plugins add top-level fields to provider requests in a prepare and accept transaction
what: Plugins can contribute additive JSON fields to official provider requests without touching messages, prompts or tool schemas; delivery is committed only after the endpoint returns HTTP 2xx and is resent later if acceptance fails.
how: DeepSeekLlmApiExtensionRegistry reserves one provider per top-level field (blank names, duplicates and collisions with base fields fail before dispatch). The adapter serializes the complete base body first, then calls prepare(request{body, signal, sessionId?, purpose?}); each provider returns a value (cloned and deep-frozen) and an optional accept(). A provider that throws or returns an uncloneable value is omitted for that request with only the first failure per field logged; only cancellation rejects. If the merged body cannot be serialized the adapter sends the base body alone and skips acceptance. After 2xx, accept() runs before the SSE body is read, failures are aggregated and logged without failing the request, and contributors resend unaccepted state next time. Fields use a reserved dsh_ prefix with an independent version per field; headers are separately documented.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane needs a governed way for features (billing tags, audit trails, ZDR flags) to annotate outbound inference calls; the prepare/accept split gives at-least-once delivery with failure isolation per contributor.
notes: Used by the default-on session-log upload (record 083) and the plugin-package inventory field; a gateway selected by baseURL receives the same fields. Acceptance means endpoint 2xx, not that the stream completed.

name: Two TypeScript programs (host and client faces) with generated contributions and per-face bundling
what: Host and browser code compile as separate programs because both merge the same Cordis Context keys, and a fixed build order generates Remote contributions on the host pass before the client pass consumes them.
how: tsconfig.json aggregates two check units, tsconfig.host.json and tsconfig.client.json ('one program cannot see both' sets of Context merges). build:lib:host runs tsc -b on the host project and then tsdown with DSH_BUILD_FACE=host, during which the Typert generator (seeded only with the host program) writes typert.host.js and typert.remote-client.js per package; build:lib:client runs tsc -b on the client project and tsdown with DSH_BUILD_FACE=client over the generated declarations without re-running the generator; package-local tsdown configs return entries for the current face, and split packages (api/gateway, api/remotes, session-controller, workspace-controller, client/connection) reference the matching leaf tsconfig.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Rust gateway plus SolidJS client can use the same discipline: generate client contracts from the server pass and forbid the two sides from sharing one type universe.
notes: Costly build graph (root build chains four phases); the payoff is declaration maps that navigate from a client call to the Host @Remote method.

name: SSH helper transport: versioned RPC with reserved management budgets and per-stream TLS-PSK
what: The SSH execution helper speaks a small versioned request, result, error and cancel protocol whose control operations cannot be starved by ordinary work, and its forwarded data streams authenticate with a per-stream key instead of certificates.
how: SSH_PROTOCOL_VERSION 2 frames {request, result, error, cancel} are validated with strict zod schemas; heartbeat, close, process.terminate and fs.streamClose have their own reserved request budgets while all other operations share the ordinary budget; a helper owns at most 128 process handles and 128 text streams. Forwarded OpenSSH sockets authenticate with TLS 1.2 PSK-AES256-GCM-SHA384 using a 256-bit per-stream capability key delivered over the administrative channel (no certificates, no cipher fallback, renegotiation disabled) so a replaced remote pathname cannot impersonate the helper. The helper runs under a client lease (default 30 s, 3 s to 600 s) and closes when the lease or channel ends; the peer never replays requests and rejects ambiguous operations on connection loss.
verevonRelevance: A reference for Verevon's remote sandbox or device agents: versioned frames, reserved control budgets, lease-based cleanup and key-bound data channels instead of host-name trust.
notes: POSIX only; no reconnect or replay (record 071). Upgrades 071 from README-level to source-verified.

name: web_search tool: bounded multi-query fan-out, round-robin merge and a standing citation instruction
what: One web_search call takes up to four queries, runs them concurrently through the active provider, and returns one merged, de-duplicated, capped source list with a standing instruction to cite URLs as markdown links.
how: parseSearchArgs requires 1 to WEB_SEARCH_MAX_QUERIES (4) non-blank queries and collapses exact duplicates; runSearchQueries calls ctx.web.search per query under a shared batch signal, so one failure aborts its siblings and the call rethrows the first failure after all settle; mergeSearchResults interleaves sources round-robin by rank, drops repeated URLs, caps at WEB_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS (8), flags truncated, and prefixes per-query provider answers with '### <query>' headings. formatSearchOutput starts with the untrusted-content notice, lists '- [label](url) - snippet (date)' lines and ends with 'Cite the relevant URLs above as markdown links in your answer.' The structured sources travel in presentationMeta so the web card replays from the log; the tool is concurrency-safe, carries a cooperative timeout (60 s for the shipped DeepSeek route) and its prompt section recommends web_fetch for full pages only when that tool is visible.
verevonRelevance: A compact blueprint for Verevon Research's first tier: fan out a few queries, merge by rank, cap, and force citation text; deeper research would add iterative planning on top, which DSH does not have.
notes: No deep-research mode, source ranking beyond provider order, or per-source credibility was found (INF); the merge keeps first-seen order per rank.

name: read_image tool: route-gated vision input through durable attachments, fail closed on unknown capability
what: The model can look at an image file in the workspace only when the exact calling route declares image input; otherwise the tool refuses before touching the filesystem.
how: read_image accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF identified by extension or, without one, by file signature (PNG, JPEG, GIF87a or GIF89a, RIFF/WEBP), with the attachment service's full decode authoritative; it runs every gate before any filesystem I/O, including a check that the active route's inputModalities contains image (an unknown capability refuses instead of waiting for an adapter failure), reads through ctx.fs, stores the bytes as a content-addressed attachment and returns an image block; oversize dimension, pixel count and byte errors stay recoverable tool errors. The tool is not registered without ctx.attachments.
verevonRelevance: Capability-gated tools that refuse early when the routed model cannot use their output save tokens and confusing provider errors; Model Plane should gate vision tools on resolved route metadata the same way.
notes: Input only: DSH has no image generation or editing, no audio or video, and no SVG, HEIC or PDF page rendering for the model (negative claims from the tool catalog and the scout's keyword sweep, INF).

name: Literal edit tool: unique-match default, intent waterfall for version guards, conditional escalation fields
what: File edits replace literal text that must match exactly once unless replace_all is set; the call is guarded by the version the agent last observed and, under a confining filesystem, can carry a justified request for a wider sandbox mode.
how: parseEditArgs rejects blank paths, empty old_string and identical old and new text; execute resolves the per-call sandbox policy first, resolves the target through ctx.fs, asks the single-slot 'fs/edit-intent' waterfall for a version guard (the observation policy returns {version} or throws FS_NOT_OBSERVED; without it the edit is an unconditional atomic edit), then calls ctx.fs.editText; sandbox denials map to the shared [sandbox: ...] marker and guarded-mutation failures to a model-facing remedy. The sandbox_permissions and justification fields appear in the schema only when the filesystem backend confines writes. The result value carries before and after text from which hunk diffs are computed for a replayable diff card; the argument order puts file_path first so UIs can show the target while arguments stream.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon coding or document-editing agents, an exact-match edit with compare-and-set guard and a before/after payload for diff review is the safest default; no patch or diff-apply tool exists to compare.
notes: Complements 072 (read-before-edit versions) and the str_replace_editor alternative; there is no multi-file patch tool in the 67-tool catalog (INF).
